The show tells us repeatedly that capitalism is cruel, yet it rarely explores why its characters ended up in such desperate situations. Curiously, the VIPs — the wealthy spectators who represent the system — are written so badly that they become almost comic. Without giving away the ending, I found the final twist more confusing than shocking.

Is it worth watching? Probably, if only to understand a global phenomenon. But for me, Squid Game is hit and miss: visually stunning and occasionally powerful, yet ultimately overrated.

5.title: Why are we fascinated by true crime?
5.brief: Write an academic essay on the popularity of true-crime documentaries and podcasts. Explain why audiences are drawn to them and discuss the ethical questions they raise.
5.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico sobre la popularidad de los documentales y pódcast de crímenes reales: por qué atraen y qué dilemas éticos plantean.
criteria: Four sentence adverbs at the start of sentences, followed by a comma (undeniably, arguably, regrettably, ultimately).
At least two “so…that” or “such…that” structures.
At least three expressions from the unit (gripping, plot twist, to binge-watch, critically acclaimed).
5.model:
True crime has become one of the most popular genres in streaming and podcasting. Documentaries about unsolved murders attract millions of viewers, and entire channels are devoted to them. Why are we so fascinated by stories that should, in theory, disturb us? This essay considers both the appeal and the ethical cost.

Undeniably, part of the appeal lies in the puzzle. A gripping case invites viewers to play detective, weighing clues and guessing the culprit before the final episode. The best series are so carefully structured that each plot twist feels both surprising and inevitable. Psychologists also suggest that watching crime from a safe distance allows us to explore fear without real danger.

Arguably, however, the genre has a darker side. Victims and their families are rarely consulted, and some productions treat real suffering as entertainment. Regrettably, the pressure to binge-watch has encouraged producers to sensationalise, dramatising details that may never have been confirmed. The result can be such an intense focus on the perpetrator that the victim is almost forgotten.

Ultimately, true crime is neither a harmless pleasure nor a moral failing. Its value depends on how responsibly it is made and how critically it is watched. Viewers who ask whose story is being told, and why, are likely to enjoy it without losing sight of the human beings behind the headlines. Producers, in turn, should treat their subjects with such respect that families would be willing to take part.

5.title: Report: attendance at the university film society
5.brief: Write a report for the student union on falling attendance at the university film society, based on a questionnaire. Present the findings and recommend changes.
5.briefEs: Escribe un informe para la unión estudiantil sobre la caída de asistencia al cineclub universitario, con base en un cuestionario.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
At least four sentence adverbs at the start of sentences (surprisingly, notably, ideally, undeniably, ultimately).
At least two “so…that” structures and two expressions from the unit (blockbuster, critically acclaimed).
5.model:
Report: Attendance at the University Film Society

Introduction
This report analyses attendance at the university film society over the current academic year and suggests ways of attracting a wider audience.

Findings
Average attendance fell from sixty-five in the first term to forty-one in the third. Attendance remained highest among first-year students. Surprisingly, the most popular screening was not a blockbuster but a critically acclaimed documentary about fishing communities, which attracted ninety people. Questionnaires completed by 120 members show that many students find the Thursday evening slot so inconvenient that they stay at home and watch films on their own. Notably, the choice of films also seems too narrow: a majority of respondents said that the programme contained too few comedies and recent releases.

Recommendations
Firstly, the society should move its screenings to Tuesday evenings, when most students have no classes. Secondly, the programme should alternate between acclaimed independent films and popular titles, so that members of every taste find something to watch. Thirdly, a short discussion after each film could be introduced. Ideally, this would be led by a lecturer from the Media Studies department.

Conclusion
Ultimately, the decline in attendance is not a sign that students have lost interest in cinema. Undeniably, they are watching films, but they prefer to do so at home. The society must therefore offer something that a screen at home cannot: company, conversation and a shared experience. These changes would be so inexpensive that they could begin next term.

5.title: An open-air film festival for our city
5.brief: Write a proposal to the city council for a free open-air film festival. Describe the concept, the programme, the budget and why it would succeed.
5.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al concejo municipal para un festival de cine al aire libre y gratuito: concepto, programación, presupuesto y por qué funcionaría.
criteria: Headings: Concept, Programme, Budget and Why it will work.
At least four sentence adverbs at the start of sentences, followed by a comma (undeniably, admittedly, crucially, interestingly, ultimately).
At least two “so…that” or “such…that” structures and two expressions from the unit (blockbuster, critically acclaimed).
5.model:
Proposal: An Open-Air Film Festival in Pasto

Concept
We propose a three-night open-air film festival in Pasto's central park, offering free screenings of recent Colombian and Latin American films. Undeniably, the city has a strong cultural life, yet residents of outlying neighbourhoods rarely have the chance to see such films on a big screen.

Programme
Each evening would begin with a short film made by local students, followed by a feature. We would select critically acclaimed titles that are accessible to a general audience, together with one blockbuster for families on the opening night. Every screening would include subtitles for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers, and a short discussion would take place afterwards with a guest speaker. Admittedly, outdoor events depend on the weather, so we would reserve the municipal auditorium as a backup.

Budget
The total budget is COP 18,000,000. Equipment hire accounts for almost half, with the remainder covering screening rights, security and publicity. The costs are so modest that the festival could be repeated every year. We will ask the city council to cover half of the costs and local businesses to sponsor the rest.

Why it will work
Crucially, the festival costs nothing to attend, so families of every income can come. The programme is so varied that it should appeal to teenagers as much as to grandparents, and the open-air setting turns each night into a community event rather than a mere screening. Interestingly, local cinemas might also benefit, since people who enjoy a film outdoors often want to see more of them. Ultimately, we believe the festival would give residents something they can be proud of.

5.title: Review: a stage thriller that almost arrives
5.brief: Write a critical review of a play or musical, real or imagined. Describe the story without spoiling it, evaluate the acting and staging, and give a rating.
5.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de una obra de teatro o musical, real o imaginada, sin revelar el final, evaluando actuaciones y puesta en escena.
criteria: Four sentence adverbs at the start of sentences, followed by a comma (admittedly, regrettably, frankly, ultimately).
At least two “so…that” or “such…that” structures.
At least three expressions from the unit (suspend disbelief, gripping, plot twist, hit and miss, to give away, overrated) and a final rating.
5.model:
The Last Tram, now playing at the Teatro Mayor, is a two-hour thriller set on a night tram in an unnamed city. Six passengers discover that the driver has vanished, and the vehicle continues to roll through the dark.

Admittedly, the premise demands that audiences suspend disbelief, but the production makes this surprisingly easy. The set is so cleverly designed that the tram seems actually to move, thanks to lighting and a rocking floor. The cast is uniformly strong, and the first act is genuinely gripping. The performance of Elena Rojas as a retired nurse who gradually takes charge is the highlight of the evening, combining authority with vulnerability.

Regrettably, the second act is hit and miss. The long-awaited plot twist, which I will not give away, is announced so heavily in advance that it loses most of its power. Several monologues, moreover, go on for such a long time that the tension drains away. Frankly, twenty minutes could be cut without any loss.

Even so, The Last Tram is far from overrated. Ultimately, its ambition and craftsmanship outweigh its flaws, and the final image is one I am unlikely to forget. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys suspense and does not mind a few slow minutes. Tickets are reasonably priced, and student discounts are available on weekdays. Three and a half stars out of five.

5.title: Request for subtitled screenings
5.brief: Write a formal letter to a cinema manager asking for regular subtitled screenings for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers. Explain the need, show the benefits for the cinema and request a meeting.
5.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal al gerente de un cine pidiendo funciones subtituladas para personas sordas o con dificultades auditivas.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Mr…, a clear request in the first paragraph, a request for a meeting and Yours sincerely.
At least four sentence adverbs at the start of sentences, followed by a comma (admittedly, crucially, regrettably, ultimately).
At least two “so…that” or “such…that” structures and a polite but firm tone.
5.model:
Dear Mr Ibarra,

I am writing on behalf of the Deaf Community Association of Pereira to request that Cine Centro offer at least one subtitled screening every week. Our association represents more than four hundred people in the region.

Admittedly, most foreign films are already shown with subtitles, but nearly all Colombian and Spanish-language productions are screened without them. Without subtitles, they simply cannot follow the dialogue. Our members love films as much as anyone. For them, this is such a significant barrier that many have stopped going to the cinema altogether. Crucially, the problem affects not only deaf people but also those who are hard of hearing, as well as many older viewers and some people learning Spanish.

We understand that scheduling is a commercial decision. However, a regular subtitled screening on a weekday evening, when the main rooms are often half empty, would cost the cinema very little and could attract a new and loyal audience. We would gladly publicise the sessions through our newsletter and social media, and we are confident that attendance would be so strong that the programme could be extended.

Regrettably, many of our members have not been to the cinema for years. Ultimately, a film is a shared experience, and we believe that everybody in the community should be able to enjoy it.

I would be glad to meet you to discuss the details, and I look forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely,
Lucía Giraldo
Deaf Community Association of Pereira

5.title: In praise of the slow film
5.brief: Write an opinion article defending slow, patient cinema in the age of streaming and short attention spans. Concede its weaknesses but argue for its value.
5.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de opinión que defienda el cine lento y pausado en la era del streaming, reconociendo sus debilidades.
criteria: Four sentence adverbs at the start of sentences, followed by a comma (admittedly, undeniably, regrettably, curiously, ultimately).
At least two “so…that” or “such…that” structures.
At least two expressions from the unit (to binge-watch, critically acclaimed) and a clear stance with one concession.
5.model:
We live in the age of the skip button. Audiences who once sat patiently through a three-hour epic now binge-watch series at double speed, and many admit that they check their phones during the dramatic scenes. I want to defend something that is rapidly disappearing: the slow film.

Admittedly, slowness can be tedious. Some films confuse emptiness with depth, and I have sat through several that were so long and so silent that I could not tell whether I was watching art or a screensaver. But the best slow films achieve something that fast ones cannot. Without constant action, we notice details: a glance across a table, the sound of rain, a character deciding not to speak.

Undeniably, streaming has made this kind of cinema harder to find. Platforms reward programmes that keep viewers watching, and algorithms promote whatever generates the most clicks. Consequently, a critically acclaimed film that builds gradually may be abandoned after ten minutes, not because it is bad, but because it demands patience. Regrettably, the market has become such a competitive place for attention that quietness is treated as a flaw.

So here is my modest proposal. Once a month, choose a film that you suspect you might find too slow. Put your phone in another room and give it forty minutes. Curiously, the films I once found dullest are now the ones I remember most vividly. Ultimately, you may be surprised by how much a patient film can give back.

6.title: Should streaming services pay musicians more?
6.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether music streaming platforms treat artists fairly and what should change.
6.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si las plataformas de música tratan justamente a los artistas.
criteria: Two double comparatives (The more…, the more…).
One use of will / would for characteristic habits.
Use “to go viral”, “a one-hit wonder” and “to sell out”.
6.model:
Never has music been so accessible. For the price of a lunch, listeners can enjoy almost every song ever recorded. Yet many musicians argue that this abundance has come at their expense.

The figures are striking. Platforms typically pay artists between 0.003 and 0.005 dollars per stream, which means that a song must be played around 250,000 times to earn the equivalent of a monthly minimum salary in Colombia. The more songs are uploaded every day — currently over 100,000 — the harder it becomes for independent musicians to stand out. Many will spend years releasing music that nobody hears, while a handful of global stars receive the vast majority of royalties.

Defenders of streaming point out that it has rescued an industry devastated by piracy. Artists who would once have depended on record labels can now reach audiences directly, and a song can go viral overnight, turning an unknown singer into a star. However, critics reply that this model encourages short, catchy tracks designed for algorithms, producing a generation of one-hit wonders rather than lasting careers.

In my view, the system needs reform. A "user-centric" payment model, in which each subscriber's money goes only to the artists they actually listen to, would be fairer to niche musicians. Platforms could also give more visibility to local talent. The more value listeners place on music, the more willing they should be to pay for it. Artists should not have to sell out to survive.

6.title: The concert I'll never forget
6.brief: Write a narrative for a music magazine's readers' section about a concert or musical experience that had a lasting impact on you.
6.briefEs: Escribe una narración sobre un concierto o experiencia musical que te marcó.
criteria: One or two double comparatives (the longer…, the louder…).
Two uses of would or will for habitual behaviour.
Use “to strike a chord”, “lyrics” and “catchy”.
6.model:
I was fourteen when my father took me to see Carlos Vives at the Parque Simón Bolívar. I had protested all week. Back then, I only listened to American pop, and vallenato, as far as I was concerned, was the music my uncles would play at family parties until three in the morning.

We arrived early, squeezed between thousands of people waving Colombian flags. When the first accordion notes rang out, I rolled my eyes. But something strange happened. The longer the concert went on, the less I wanted to pretend I wasn't enjoying it. The rhythm was catchy, of course, but it was the lyrics that struck a chord — songs about the Sierra Nevada, the rivers and the small towns my father had grown up in.

At one point, Vives sang "La Tierra del Olvido", and I looked at my father. He was crying. I had never seen him cry before. He told me later that his own father used to sing that song while working in the fields.

That night changed my relationship with music. The more I listened to vallenato and cumbia, the more I understood where I came from. These days, I will often put on an old Diomedes Díaz album while I cook, and my American pop playlists gather dust.

My father still teases me about it. "You came for me," he says, "but you stayed for the accordion."

6.title: What defines musical success?
6.brief: Write an article for a cultural website discussing what “success” means for a musician today: fame, money, critical acclaim or longevity.
6.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre qué significa el éxito para un músico hoy: fama, dinero, crítica o permanencia.
criteria: Two double comparatives and one “would” for past habits.
Use “to fade into obscurity”, “to stand the test of time” and “derivative”.
A title, clear sections or paragraphs, and a thought-provoking ending.
6.model:
What Does It Mean to "Make It" in Music?

Ask a teenager what makes a musician successful, and the answer will probably be measured in numbers: followers, streams, views. Yet the history of music suggests that numbers alone tell a very incomplete story.

Consider fame. Every year, dozens of songs go viral and accumulate billions of plays, only for their creators to fade into obscurity within months. The faster an artist rises, it often seems, the faster they fall. Money is an equally unreliable measure. Many of the highest-earning performers today produce music that critics dismiss as derivative, while some of the most influential artists in history died poor. Van Gogh's story has musical equivalents: Nick Drake, for instance, sold fewer than 5,000 albums in his lifetime and is now regarded as a genius.

Critical acclaim offers another perspective, but critics are not infallible. In the 1960s, many reviewers would describe rock and roll as noise that would never last.

Perhaps the truest test of success is longevity: music that stands the test of time. Songs by Totó la Momposina or Joe Arroyo continue to fill dance floors decades after they were recorded, not because an algorithm recommends them, but because they still mean something to people.

The more I think about it, the more convinced I become that success cannot be reduced to a single metric. A musician who moves a small audience deeply may have achieved more than one who entertains millions briefly. Fame is loud; influence is quiet — and it lasts much longer.

6.title: Why does music bring memories back so vividly?
6.brief: Write an academic essay exploring why music is such a powerful trigger of memory. Present at least two explanations and acknowledge what remains uncertain.
6.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico que explore por qué la música despierta recuerdos con tanta fuerza, con al menos dos explicaciones y lo que aún se desconoce.
criteria: At least two double comparatives (The more…, the more…; The longer…, the more…).
At least two uses of will or would for habits or typical behaviour (People will often say…).
At least three expressions from the unit (catchy, lyrics, to strike a chord) and hedged claims (may, tends to, probably).
6.model:
Most people can recall a song that instantly transports them to a particular summer, a first dance or a funeral. This link between music and memory is so common that we rarely stop to question it. Yet scientists are still working out why a few seconds of melody can bring back an entire scene. This essay considers some explanations and their limits.

One explanation is emotional. Music activates areas of the brain associated with feeling, and the more intense the emotion at the time of listening, the more firmly the memory is stored. Songs from adolescence strike a chord especially deeply, probably because that period is full of first experiences. People will often say that the music of their teens is better than anything produced since, which suggests that memory, rather than quality, is doing much of the work.

A second explanation is repetition. A catchy chorus that we heard every day on the radio becomes, in a sense, part of our daily routine. The more often a song was played, the deeper its connection to the surrounding events tends to be. Older relatives would often hum the same tunes while cooking, and for many of us those melodies now evoke kitchens and family meals rather than any particular concert.

Neither explanation is complete. The longer researchers study the question, the more variables they discover, from personality to culture. What can be said with confidence is that music is a uniquely efficient trigger. That may explain why therapists increasingly use familiar songs with people suffering from dementia, who will sometimes recall the lyrics of songs they heard decades ago.

6.title: Report: listening habits of secondary students
6.brief: Write a report for a head teacher on a survey of students' music-listening habits. Present the findings, draw conclusions and recommend action.
6.briefEs: Escribe un informe para la dirección de un colegio sobre una encuesta acerca de los hábitos de escucha musical de los estudiantes.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
At least two double comparatives (The more…, the more…) and at least two uses of will or would for habits.
At least two expressions from the unit (go viral, lyrics) in an impersonal, objective register.
6.model:
Report: Listening Habits of Secondary Students

Introduction
This report summarises the results of a survey on the listening habits of 200 secondary students at a school in Bucaramanga. Its aim is to find out how students discover music and whether those habits affect their concentration.

Findings
The great majority of students, 91 per cent, listen to music every day, mostly through streaming platforms. Many will listen for more than three hours, usually while travelling or doing homework. Students reported that they would often discover a new song through a short video that had gone viral, and then play it repeatedly for a few days. The more time students spent online, the more likely they were to say that their taste changed quickly. Interestingly, 40 per cent claimed that music helped them to concentrate, whereas teachers observed that students who listened to lyrics while studying tended to work more slowly. Only 12 per cent could name the title of a song that was more than twenty years old.

Recommendations
We recommend that the school organise a listening club in which students present songs from different decades, since the more varied their listening, the more flexible their taste is likely to become. Teachers should also encourage students to choose instrumental music when studying. Finally, the survey should be repeated next year to see whether habits have changed.

Conclusion
Students listen to a great deal of music, but mostly to what an algorithm recommends. The longer they remain inside these recommendations, the less likely they are to meet anything unfamiliar. A modest, school-based intervention could help to widen their horizons.

6.title: An instrument library for young musicians
6.brief: Write a proposal to a community centre for a library that lends musical instruments to teenagers who cannot afford their own. Explain the need, the plan, the budget and the expected results.
6.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a un centro comunitario para una biblioteca que preste instrumentos musicales a adolescentes sin recursos.
criteria: Headings: Background, Proposal, Budget and Expected outcomes.
At least two double comparatives (The more…, the more…; The longer…, the less…).
At least one use of will or would for habits (Beginners will often give up…) and one expression from the unit (to sell out, catchy, to strike a chord).
6.model:
Proposal: An Instrument Library for Young Musicians

Background
Many teenagers in our neighbourhood want to learn an instrument, but the cost of buying one is prohibitive. A basic acoustic guitar costs around COP 300,000, which is more than many families can spend. Meanwhile, hundreds of instruments sit unused in cupboards and attics. The longer a child waits for an instrument, the less likely he or she is to learn.

Proposal
We propose creating a lending library, in which residents would donate instruments they no longer use and young people could borrow them for three months at a time. A volunteer technician would repair each instrument before it is lent, and weekly workshops would be run by local musicians. Beginners will often give up within a few weeks unless they have regular support, so the workshops are an essential part of the plan.

Budget
The main cost is the refurbishment of donated instruments, estimated at COP 2,500,000 for the first year, together with a small stipend for the workshop leaders. The community centre has offered a room free of charge.

Expected outcomes
We expect around sixty young people to take part in the first year. The more instruments the library collects, the more young people it can serve, and the more visible music becomes in the neighbourhood. Learning together, young people will often form friendships that last well beyond the course. At the end of each term, students would perform for their families, so that the effort they have made is recognised. We would be delighted if the first end-of-term concert were to sell out.

6.title: Review: Salt and Static, a debut album
6.brief: Write a critical review of a debut album, real or imagined. Comment on the songs, the lyrics and the production, and say who would enjoy it.
6.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de un álbum debut, real o imaginado: canciones, letras y producción, y a quién le gustaría.
criteria: At least two double comparatives (The further…, the more…; The more polished…, the less…).
At least one use of will or would for typical behaviour (Fans will play it again and again).
At least four expressions from the unit (catchy, lyrics, to strike a chord, derivative, one-hit wonder, to stand the test of time, to go viral) and a final rating.
6.model:
Salt and Static, the debut album by Colombian singer-songwriter Inés Barrera, arrives with considerable buzz. Two of its singles went viral last summer, and tickets for her first tour have already sold out. The record has twelve tracks and lasts just under forty minutes. The question is whether the album justifies the excitement.

In large part, it does. The title track, with its catchy guitar riff, is the kind of song that will stay in your head for days, and the lyrics, about leaving a coastal town, strike a chord without sounding sentimental. The further the record progresses, the more confident Barrera's voice becomes, and the quieter the arrangements, the more memorable the songs.

However, the album is not without problems. Several tracks in the middle sound derivative, borrowing heavily from the sound of her influences. The producer seems to have been so keen to create another hit that he has smoothed away the roughness that made her early recordings so appealing. I found myself wanting to hear her take more risks. The more polished the production becomes, the less distinctive she sounds.

Even so, this is an impressive debut, and Barrera is clearly no one-hit wonder. Fans of intelligent, melodic pop will play it again and again, and I suspect that its best songs will stand the test of time. Listeners tired of manufactured hits should give it a chance. Four stars out of five.

6.title: Permission for a community concert
6.brief: Write a formal letter to the municipal authorities requesting permission to hold a free open-air concert. Explain who is organising it, what the programme will be and what guarantees you offer.
6.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal a las autoridades municipales pidiendo permiso para un concierto gratuito al aire libre.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Ms…, a clear request in the opening sentence, enclosures and Yours sincerely.
At least two double comparatives (The more often…, the more…) and at least one use of will or would for habitual behaviour.
At least one expression from the unit (to strike a chord, catchy, to sell out) and a polite, confident tone.
6.model:
Dear Ms Arango,

I am writing to request permission to hold a free community concert in the central square on Saturday 13 June, from four until eight o'clock in the evening.

The concert would be organised by the youth orchestra of the Escuela de Música Municipal, which I have directed for six years. Last year, our performances at the school drew audiences so large that many people had to stand outside. The more often we perform, the more people ask us to play in public spaces, and we would like to respond to this demand. Local families will often arrive an hour early to secure a place, which shows how much the orchestra means to the neighbourhood.

The programme would include a mixture of classical pieces and arrangements of popular songs. We believe that the more familiar the repertoire, the more welcoming the atmosphere will be for people who have never attended a concert. We would take full responsibility for the stage, the sound equipment and the removal of rubbish, and we would arrange for six volunteers to help with crowd control. Entry would be free, and no alcohol would be sold. We hope the music will strike a chord with listeners of every age.

I enclose a letter of support from the school's head teacher and a plan of the proposed layout. Should any further documentation be required, please let me know, and I will provide it without delay. I would be happy to meet you or your colleagues in the planning department.

Thank you for considering this request. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Martín Cifuentes
Director, Youth Orchestra

6.title: Twenty years of a neighbourhood music school
6.brief: Write a speech for the twentieth anniversary of a community music school. Recall the early days, say what the school has taught and thank the audience.
6.briefEs: Escribe un discurso para el vigésimo aniversario de una escuela de música comunitaria: recuerda los inicios, lo que ha enseñado y agradece al público.
criteria: At least two double comparatives (The longer…, the more…; the more…, the better…).
At least three uses of would or will for habits (children would arrive…, older students will always stay behind…).
At least two expressions from the unit (to go viral, to sell out, to strike a chord) and a spoken register with direct address.
6.model:
Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the twentieth birthday of the Escuela de Música del Barrio.

When we opened in a borrowed garage, we had six guitars, one drum kit and no money. Every afternoon, children would arrive straight from school, and we would play until the neighbours complained. Mrs Ortega from number twelve would knock on the wall at six o'clock, and we would ignore her until she brought us coffee.

The longer I think about those years, the more I realise what the school has really taught. It has taught patience: the more a student practises, the better she plays, and there are no shortcuts. It has also taught generosity. Our older students will always stay behind to help the younger ones, and nobody has ever asked them to.

Some of you have gone on to become professional musicians. One of our graduates now plays in an orchestra abroad, and another had a song that went viral last year, which is a very modern way of becoming famous. But most of you will never sell out a stadium, and that is perfectly fine. A song that strikes a chord with a single listener is a success.

So tonight, I ask you to do two things. Listen carefully, because the music you will hear was written by children who are now adults. And please, applaud loudly, because applause is the only wage our young musicians will accept.

Thank you, and happy birthday to us all.

7.title: Is nostalgia holding us back?
7.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether nostalgia for “the good old days” is harmless comfort or an obstacle to progress.
7.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si la nostalgia por “los viejos tiempos” es un consuelo inofensivo o un obstáculo.
criteria: Relative clauses where the pronoun is optional and where it is required (omitted in at least one).
Two comparisons with as if / as though / the way / like.
Use “nostalgia”, “to hark back to” and “with hindsight”.
7.model:
Every generation seems convinced that life was better before. Our grandparents talk about the days when neighbours left their doors open; our parents remember a childhood without screens. But is this nostalgia a harmless pleasure, or does it prevent us from embracing change?

There is no doubt that nostalgia serves a purpose. Psychologists have found that recalling happy memories can reduce loneliness and give people a sense of continuity in a world that changes at bewildering speed. The songs we listened to as teenagers, the food our mothers cooked, the streets we played in — these connect us to who we were. Speaking about the past the way our elders do is also a means of passing values from one generation to the next.

However, nostalgia can distort reality. Many people talk about the 1980s as if they had been a golden age, forgetting the violence, the inequality and the lack of opportunities that characterised those years in Colombia. With hindsight, the past often looks simpler than it really was, simply because we were children and others solved our problems for us. Politicians who hark back to an idealised past frequently use this sentiment to resist necessary reforms, from women's rights to environmental protection.

The healthiest approach, it seems to me, is to treat nostalgia like a photograph rather than a map. We can look at it with affection, but we should not use it to decide where to go next. The past we remember is, after all, partly one we have invented.

7.title: A milestone that shaped me
7.brief: Write a reflective personal essay about a rite of passage or milestone that marked your transition into adulthood.
7.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo personal reflexivo sobre un rito de paso o hito que marcó tu entrada a la adultez.
criteria: Three relative clauses, including one with the pronoun omitted and one with a preposition (in which / whom).
Two clauses with as if, as though or like.
Use “a rite of passage”, “formative” and “to look back on”.
7.model:
In many cultures, the rite of passage into adulthood is a ceremony: a quinceañera, a graduation, a first communion. Mine was far less glamorous. It was the night I spent alone in a hospital waiting room at the age of nineteen.

My mother, with whom I had always had a difficult relationship, collapsed at work and was taken to the emergency room. My father was travelling, and my older brother lived abroad, so the decisions the doctors needed fell to me. I remember signing forms I barely understood, talking to nurses as though I knew what I was doing, and calling relatives in a voice that sounded like someone else's.

She recovered, thankfully. But something had shifted. For the first time, I saw my mother not as an authority figure but as a person who was vulnerable and frightened, just like me. In the weeks that followed, we talked in a way we never had before.

When I look back on that period, I realise how formative it was. The person I had been — impatient, convinced that my parents owed me everything — did not survive that night. In his place was someone who understood that caring for others is not a burden but a responsibility we inherit.

People sometimes describe adulthood as if it were a destination you reach at eighteen. In my experience, it arrives without warning, in a corridor that smells of disinfectant, at three o'clock in the morning.

7.title: The generation gap at work
7.brief: Write a report for a company's human resources department on the challenges and benefits of having several generations working together, with recommendations.
7.briefEs: Escribe un informe para recursos humanos sobre los retos y beneficios de que varias generaciones trabajen juntas.
criteria: Headings, impersonal register and recommendations.
Relative clauses with required and optional pronouns, including “whose”.
Use “generation gap” and one structure with “the way”.
7.model:
Report: Managing a Multigenerational Workforce

Introduction
The aim of this report is to examine how the generation gap affects collaboration in our company, in which employees range in age from 19 to 67. It draws on a staff survey and four focus groups.

Challenges
The main difficulties identified relate to communication. Older employees, whose careers began before email, generally prefer face-to-face meetings and phone calls, whereas younger staff favour instant messaging. Several participants complained about the way colleagues of other ages reply to messages, describing them as either "too formal" or "rude". There are also differing expectations regarding working hours: the flexibility that younger employees value is sometimes perceived by senior managers as a lack of commitment.

Benefits
Despite these tensions, mixed teams were found to perform better on complex projects. Employees with decades of experience contribute knowledge of clients and industry history that cannot be learned from manuals, while recent graduates bring digital skills and fresh perspectives. Many respondents said the colleague they had learned most from was someone from a different generation.

Recommendations
• A reverse mentoring scheme should be introduced, in which junior staff teach digital tools to senior colleagues and vice versa.
• Teams should agree explicitly on preferred communication channels and response times.
• Training on unconscious age bias should be offered to all managers.

Conclusion
Age diversity is an asset which, if managed thoughtfully, can strengthen both innovation and staff loyalty.

7.title: Must traditions change in order to survive?
7.brief: Write an academic essay on whether cultural traditions must adapt to survive or should be preserved exactly as they are. Use at least one concrete example.
7.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico sobre si las tradiciones culturales deben adaptarse para sobrevivir o conservarse tal como son.
criteria: Relative clauses with the pronoun omitted at least once, one with “whose” and one with a preposition + whom or which.
At least two comparisons with as if, as though, the way or like.
At least three expressions from the unit (nostalgia, upbringing, with hindsight, to look back on, to hark back to).
7.model:
Traditions are often presented as fixed inheritances, practices that must be preserved exactly as our ancestors performed them. The reality is more complicated. Customs which seem ancient have frequently been reinvented, and those that survive are usually the ones that have adapted. This essay argues that change is not a threat to tradition but a condition of its survival.

Consider the carnival of Barranquilla, which UNESCO has recognised as part of humanity's intangible heritage. Its dances and costumes, which draw on African, indigenous and European influences, have never stopped evolving. Each generation adds new characters and satirical themes, so that the festival speaks to the people who take part in it, rather than merely commemorating the past.

Nevertheless, there is a point at which change becomes erosion. When a ritual is performed purely for tourists, as if it were a show with no meaning beyond the ticket price, the community whose heritage it represents may feel dispossessed. The people to whom a tradition matters most should therefore decide how it evolves, and the decisions they take should not be dictated by commercial convenience.

Looking back on one's own upbringing, it is easy to feel nostalgia for rituals that have disappeared and to treat them as though they had been perfect. With hindsight, however, many of them were less innocent than we remember. The traditions worth keeping are those that still serve the people who practise them. Those that cannot adapt will fade; those that can will, in a new form, outlive us all.

7.title: Report: an oral history project with older residents
7.brief: Write a report on a school project in which students interviewed older residents about their lives. Describe the method, the findings and your recommendations.
7.briefEs: Escribe un informe sobre un proyecto escolar en el que estudiantes entrevistaron a residentes mayores: método, hallazgos y recomendaciones.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Method, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion (a short one is enough).
Relative clauses with the pronoun omitted at least once, plus “whom”, “whose” and “where”.
At least one comparison with as if and one with the way, and the expression “generation gap”.
7.model:
Report: An Oral History Project with Older Residents

Introduction
This report describes a project in which twelve secondary students interviewed older residents of the neighbourhood about their lives during the 1960s and 1970s. The aim was to preserve memories that might otherwise be lost and to bring generations closer together.

Method
Each student interviewed one resident, whom they met three times over two months. Interviews, which lasted about an hour, were recorded with the interviewee's consent. Students then wrote a short account of the story they had heard.

Findings
Residents described a childhood in which families had little money but strong community ties. Several spoke of the street where they grew up as if it had been a single large household. Students were struck by the way their interviewees remembered small details, such as the smell of a bakery or the name of a teacher who had once changed their lives. Many participants admitted that they had never been asked about their past before. The gap in experience was wide: for older residents, a telephone was a luxury they had waited years to own. For the students, whose lives revolve around their phones, this was almost unimaginable.

Recommendations
We recommend that the school repeat the project next year and that the recordings be stored in the municipal library, where future researchers can consult them. Students who took part should be asked to present their stories at a public event, to which the interviewees and their families would be welcome.

Conclusion
The project showed that the generation gap is narrower than it appears, provided that each side is willing to listen.

7.title: A cooking workshop for three generations
7.brief: Write a proposal to a community centre for a monthly workshop in which teenagers and older residents cook traditional dishes together. Explain the need, the plan, the resources and the expected outcomes.
7.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a un centro comunitario para un taller mensual donde adolescentes y adultos mayores cocinen platos tradicionales juntos.
criteria: Headings: Background, Proposal, Resources and Expected outcomes.
Relative clauses with the pronoun omitted at least once, plus “whose” and a non-defining clause with “which”.
At least one comparison with as though and one with the way, and two expressions from the unit (upbringing, generation gap, to look back on).
7.model:
Proposal: A Cooking Workshop for Three Generations

Background
In our neighbourhood, young people and older residents rarely spend time together. Grandparents often feel as though their knowledge is no longer valued, while teenagers, whose weekends are dominated by screens, miss the chance to learn skills that are in danger of disappearing. Traditional cooking, which embodies the history of every family, is a clear example.

Proposal
We propose a monthly cooking workshop in which pairs made up of a teenager and an older resident prepare a traditional dish together. The recipes would be chosen by the older participants, and the young people would record the process in writing and on video. At the end of the year, the recipes would be gathered into a small book which every family could keep. The workshops would take place in the school kitchen, the only space in the area that has the equipment we need.

Resources
The costs are modest. Ingredients for twelve workshops will cost approximately COP 1,800,000, and printing the recipe book about COP 900,000. The school has agreed to lend the kitchen, and a local supermarket, which has supported similar events, has offered a discount.

Expected outcomes
We expect the workshops to build friendships that would not otherwise exist. Teenagers will gain a new respect for the people who raised the neighbourhood, and older participants will feel that their upbringing and experience still matter. Taking part may also help young people look back on their own family history with more curiosity. Above all, the project would show that the generation gap is something we can cross, sharing food the way families have always done.

7.title: Review: a memoir of growing up
7.brief: Write a critical review of a memoir, real or imagined, about childhood and family. Evaluate the voice, the structure and the portrayal of different generations.
7.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de unas memorias, reales o imaginadas, sobre la infancia y la familia.
criteria: Relative clauses with the pronoun omitted at least once, plus “whose” and a non-defining clause with “which”.
At least two comparisons with as if, as though or the way.
At least two expressions from the unit (with hindsight, to hark back to, upbringing, formative) and a final rating.
7.model:
The House on Calle Sexta, the first book by Amparo Velásquez, is a memoir of growing up in a crowded family home in 1980s Cali. It runs to two hundred and ten pages. Told in short, vivid chapters, it recreates a world in which three generations shared one roof, one bathroom and, apparently, one opinion about everything.

The book's greatest strength is its voice. Velásquez writes about her grandmother, whose strictness she resented as a child, with a tenderness that grows the more she understands her. Her description of the day she left home, which she presents as though it were a minor event, is quietly devastating. The reader senses everything she does not say.

Less successful are the chapters set in her adult years. Here the narrative loses focus, and the author, who writes so convincingly about the past, seems uncertain about the present. With hindsight, the book might have been stronger if it had ended where the childhood ends. There is also a tendency to hark back to the neighbourhood as if it had been a lost paradise, which sits uneasily with the poverty she herself describes.

Nevertheless, this is a moving and honest debut. Readers who enjoy family stories, or who simply want to understand the way ordinary people live through history, will find much to admire. It is a book you will finish in a weekend and think about for much longer. Four stars out of five.

7.title: Objection to the demolition of a market hall
7.brief: Write a formal letter to the city council objecting to the planned demolition of an old market hall. Explain what the place means to the community and propose an alternative.
7.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal al concejo objetando la demolición de una antigua plaza de mercado: qué significa para la comunidad y una alternativa.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Sir or Madam, a clear objection in the opening sentence, a specific request and Yours faithfully.
Relative clauses with the pronoun omitted at least once, plus “whose” and “with whom” or “to whom”.
At least one comparison with as though and one expression from the unit (upbringing, nostalgia, generation gap).
7.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to object to the council's plan to demolish the old market hall on Calle 8, a building which has served the community for almost ninety years.

The market is, for many of us, far more than a place where we buy vegetables. It is the place where I first learned to haggle, under the supervision of a grandmother who treated every purchase as though it were a matter of national importance. It is, in the full sense of the word, part of our upbringing. The stallholders, many of whose families have worked there for generations, know their customers by name. Such relationships cannot be moved to a shopping centre, however modern it may be.

I understand that the building needs repair, and I do not suggest that nothing should change. However, the report the council commissioned considers only the cost of renovation, not the social value of what would be lost. The people who rely on the market most, including elderly residents and low-income families, have not been consulted.

I would therefore ask the council to postpone its decision until a full public consultation has been held. I also propose that the possibility of restoring the existing hall, with funds from the national heritage programme, be examined properly. Should you wish, I would be glad to put you in touch with the stallholders' association, with whom I have been in regular contact.

Thank you for your attention. I trust that the council will reconsider.

Yours faithfully,
Fabiola Nieto

7.title: A birthday speech for my grandmother
7.brief: Write a speech for your grandmother's eightieth birthday. Describe what she has taught you, how her life differs from yours and why you admire her.
7.briefEs: Escribe un discurso para el cumpleaños ochenta de tu abuela: lo que te ha enseñado, cómo su vida difiere de la tuya y por qué la admiras.
criteria: Relative clauses with the pronoun omitted at least once, plus “whose” and “where”.
At least two comparisons with as if, as though or the way.
At least two expressions from the unit (generation gap, to settle down, upbringing) and a spoken register with a closing toast.
7.model:
Good evening, family and friends. For those who do not know me, I am Julia's granddaughter, which is the best job I have ever had.

Tonight we are celebrating eighty years of a woman who has taught me almost everything I know. The first thing she taught me was how to make arepas, which she does as though she were conducting an orchestra. The second thing was how to stand up for myself, a lesson she delivered the way she does everything: firmly, kindly and with a wooden spoon in her hand.

My grandmother grew up in a village where there was no electricity, in a family whose members measured wealth in harvests rather than money. She settled down in Bogotá at nineteen, a city she had never seen, and raised four children while working nights in a factory. When I ask her how she managed, she shrugs as if it were nothing.

My grandmother's generation sometimes seems distant from mine, but there is no real generation gap in this family. She has never told me what to think. She has simply shown me how to live: with humour, courage and a deep respect for the people who share our table.

Abuela, I hope that when I am eighty, someone will say about me what we all say about you tonight: that she made everyone feel at home.

Please raise your glasses to Julia. Happy birthday, Abuela, and thank you for everything.

8.title: Is advertising to children ethical?
8.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether advertising aimed at children should be banned or more strictly regulated.
8.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si la publicidad dirigida a niños debería prohibirse o regularse más.
criteria: Two subjunctive structures (It is essential that companies be…, insist that…).
Correct placement of direct and indirect objects (sell children products / sell products to children).
Use “target audience”, “consumerism” and “brand loyalty”.
8.model:
Children have become one of the most lucrative target audiences in the world. Companies spend billions every year trying to sell them products, from sugary cereals to video games, and to build brand loyalty that will last a lifetime. Should this be allowed?

Those who defend children's advertising argue that it is a legitimate part of a market economy. Adverts inform families about new products, and they fund much of the free content children enjoy, from television programmes to online videos. Moreover, they insist that parents, not governments, should decide what their children are exposed to.

However, this argument overlooks a crucial fact: young children cannot distinguish between entertainment and persuasion. Research suggests that, until about the age of eight, most children believe that adverts simply tell the truth. Promoting junk food to them has been linked to rising rates of childhood obesity, and influencers who show children toys in "unboxing" videos often fail to make clear that they are being paid. Encouraging consumerism from such an early age also places enormous pressure on low-income families, whose children may feel excluded when they cannot buy what their friends have.

In my view, it is essential that advertising to young children be strictly regulated. Several countries, including Chile and Norway, have already banned marketing unhealthy food to under-14s, with encouraging results. I would recommend that Colombia adopt similar measures, and that platforms be required to label sponsored content clearly. Childhood should be a time for play, not a marketing opportunity.

8.title: Review: a product that didn't live up to the hype
8.brief: Write a detailed review for a consumer website of a product you bought because of clever marketing, explaining why it was a false economy.
8.briefEs: Escribe una reseña para un sitio de consumidores sobre un producto que compraste por el marketing y resultó mala inversión.
criteria: Two sentences with indirect objects in different positions (gave me a discount / gave it to me).
One subjunctive (I would suggest that buyers be…).
Use “impulse buy”, “to be sold on” and “a false economy”.
8.model:
★★☆☆☆ "The last blender you'll ever need" — or not

I'll admit it: this blender was an impulse buy. I was scrolling late at night when an advert showed me a smiling chef crushing ice, nuts and frozen fruit in seconds. A countdown timer promised me a 40% discount if I ordered within ten minutes. I was sold on it before I had even read the specifications.

The first week was promising. The design is elegant and the machine is surprisingly quiet. However, problems appeared quickly. The jug is made of thin plastic that cracked after a month of daily smoothies, and the "powerful" motor struggles with anything harder than a banana. When I contacted customer service, they offered me a replacement jug — but only if I paid the shipping, which cost almost as much as the jug itself.

What frustrates me most is the marketing. The "40% discount" turned out to be the product's normal price; the timer resets every time you open the page. The lifetime guarantee that the website advertises applies only to the motor, and only if you register within seven days.

In the end, this cheap blender proved a false economy. I have since bought a sturdier model from a well-known brand, which cost twice as much but has worked perfectly for a year.

My advice: ignore the countdown timers. I would suggest that buyers be especially wary of products sold exclusively through social media adverts.

8.title: A letter to the editor about consumerism
8.brief: Write a letter to a newspaper editor responding to an article that praised Black Friday as “good for the economy”. Present a counter-argument.
8.briefEs: Escribe una carta al editor respondiendo a un artículo que elogiaba el Black Friday como “bueno para la economía”.
criteria: Formal letter conventions and a clear position.
Two subjunctive structures (I propose that…, It is vital that…).
Use “disposable income”, “to drive up” and “consumerism”.
8.model:
Dear Editor,

I read with interest last Sunday's article "Black Friday: A Gift for the Economy", in which your columnist argued that the annual shopping event benefits Colombian businesses and consumers alike. While I do not dispute that retailers enjoy a surge in sales, I believe the article presented a dangerously incomplete picture.

Firstly, many of the so-called bargains are illusory. Consumer organisations have repeatedly shown that some shops drive up prices in the weeks before the event in order to offer apparently spectacular discounts. Secondly, the pressure to buy encourages families to spend money they do not have. For households with little disposable income, credit-card debt taken on in November can last well into the following year.

There is also an environmental cost that the article ignored entirely. Much of what is purchased — cheap electronics, fast fashion — is discarded within months, contributing to the mountains of waste our cities already struggle to manage.

I am not suggesting that shopping is inherently wrong. However, a newspaper that celebrates unrestrained consumerism without acknowledging its consequences does its readers a disservice. I propose that your paper publish practical advice on recognising false discounts, and it is vital that the government require shops to display the lowest price charged in the previous thirty days, as is now the rule in the European Union.

Yours faithfully,
Mariana Ochoa
Bucaramanga

8.title: Buy now, pay later: convenience or trap?
8.brief: Write an academic essay on whether “buy now, pay later” payment schemes help consumers or encourage debt. Present both views and say how the schemes should be regulated.
8.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico sobre si los sistemas de “compra ahora, paga después” ayudan a los consumidores o fomentan el endeudamiento.
criteria: At least three subjunctive structures (insist that… be…, It is essential that… be…, recommend that… show…).
Direct and indirect objects in both patterns (offer customers a discount / offer a discount to customers).
At least two expressions from the unit (disposable income, false economy, impulse buy, drive up).
8.model:
Buy now, pay later schemes allow shoppers to divide a purchase into small instalments, usually without interest. Retailers offer customers this option at checkout in the hope of increasing sales, and many young people, whose disposable income is limited, find it irresistible. But is it a convenient tool or a trap?

Defenders point out that the schemes spare buyers the high interest rates of credit cards. A student who needs a laptop can spread the cost over several months and give the lender nothing but the original price, provided that every payment is made on time. Moreover, because the process is quick, it makes consumers feel that they are in control of their finances.

Critics, however, argue that this feeling is deceptive. Instalments make a purchase appear cheaper than it is, and shoppers tend to buy more than they would otherwise. A single late payment can bring heavy fees, and several small debts may accumulate without the borrower noticing. For this reason, many consumer organisations insist that these schemes be regulated in the same way as other forms of credit. They also recommend that retailers show customers the total cost before the transaction is completed.

In my view, the schemes are neither good nor bad in themselves. It is essential, however, that buyers be fully informed and that companies not exploit their impatience. Teachers could help by showing pupils how interest and fees work, and governments by requiring lenders to offer clear warnings to borrowers. Without such safeguards, what is marketed as convenience may become a false economy.

8.title: Executive summary: spending habits of university students
8.brief: Write the executive summary of a report on a survey about how university students spend money. State the purpose, the key findings and your recommendations to the student welfare office.
8.briefEs: Escribe el resumen ejecutivo de un informe sobre una encuesta acerca de cómo gastan dinero los universitarios, con recomendaciones.
criteria: Headings: Purpose, Key findings, Recommendations and Next steps.
At least three subjunctive structures (recommend that… run, advisable that… offer, propose that… be reviewed).
Direct and indirect objects in both patterns (offer students an app / bring tools to the attention of students) and at least two expressions from the unit (impulse buy, disposable income).
8.model:
Executive Summary: Spending Habits of University Students

Purpose
This summary presents the main results of a survey of 300 university students about how they spend their money and what influences their purchases. The survey was carried out online in September. It is intended for the student welfare office, which has asked us for practical recommendations.

Key findings
Most students have little disposable income, and 64 per cent said that they had made at least one impulse buy in the previous month. The commonest purchases were clothes, snacks and subscriptions. Students reported that online advertisements often send them discounts which they cannot resist, and that friends' recommendations carry more weight than any other source. Almost a third admitted that they had lent a friend money which was never returned. Only 20 per cent kept a written budget.

Recommendations
We recommend that the welfare office run short workshops on budgeting during the first week of term. It is also advisable that the university offer students a free budgeting app, preferably one that can be linked to a bank account, and that it bring these tools to the attention of new students through the orientation programme. We further suggest that the student shop give members a loyalty card, which would reward regular customers without encouraging them to buy more than they need.

Next steps
If the proposals are approved, the first workshops could start in February. We propose that their effect be reviewed after one semester, so that the programme can be improved or, if necessary, discontinued.

8.title: A library of things for our neighbourhood
8.brief: Write a proposal for a neighbourhood “library of things” where residents can borrow tools and equipment instead of buying them. Explain the need, the plan, the costs and the benefits.
8.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta para una “biblioteca de cosas” de barrio donde los vecinos presten herramientas y equipos en lugar de comprarlos.
criteria: Headings: Background, Proposal, Costs and Expected benefits.
At least three subjunctive structures (propose that… lend, It is essential that… be checked, suggest that… manage).
Direct and indirect objects in both patterns (give us stock / hand out items to members) and at least two expressions from the unit (false economy, consumerism).
8.model:
Proposal: A Library of Things for Our Neighbourhood

Background
Most households own tools and equipment that are used only a handful of times a year: drills, ladders, camping gear, sewing machines. Buying such items new is expensive, and storing them takes space. We believe that a neighbourhood library of things could save residents money and reduce waste at the same time.

Proposal
We propose that the library lend items to members for up to one week, free of charge. Residents could donate equipment they no longer need, and local businesses might give us surplus stock, which we would hand out only to registered members. It is essential that every item be checked before it is lent, and that borrowers return it in the same condition. We suggest that a volunteer committee manage the catalogue and that it explain the rules to new members during a short induction. Members would show their card to the volunteer on duty, who would then hand them the item.

Costs
Start-up costs are low. Shelving and insurance will cost around COP 3,500,000, and a simple software system for the catalogue, about COP 600,000. The parish hall has offered us a storeroom, so we will not need to pay rent.

Expected benefits
A household that borrows a drill instead of buying one avoids a false economy, since the cost of a new tool is rarely justified by occasional use. We expect at least two hundred members within a year, and we recommend that the council recognise the project as a community service. Reducing the pressure to buy things we use once may even weaken the habit of consumerism.

8.title: Review: a book against buying too much
8.brief: Write a critical review of a book, real or imagined, that questions consumer culture. Evaluate its arguments, its style and its practical advice.
8.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de un libro, real o imaginado, que cuestione la cultura de consumo: argumentos, estilo y consejos prácticos.
criteria: At least two subjunctive structures (insists that readers give up, recommend that consumers be encouraged, suggest that anyone read).
Direct and indirect objects in both patterns (sell children products / sell products to children; offer customers a discount).
At least three expressions from the unit (brand loyalty, bargain, impulse buy) and a final rating.
8.model:
Enough, Thank You, the new book by journalist Valeria Montoya, begins with a confession: the author spent a year trying not to buy anything new, and failed in the third week. What follows is a funny, sharply observed account of life in a society that sells us dreams as often as it sells us products.

Montoya is at her best when she examines the tricks of modern marketing. She describes how supermarkets arrange shelves so that the most profitable goods are placed at eye level, and how online shops offer customers a discount that disappears if they leave the page. I was particularly struck by her chapter on brand loyalty, in which she shows how companies sell children products they will keep buying for decades.

The book is less convincing when it turns to advice. Montoya insists that readers give up shopping altogether, a demand which will strike many as unrealistic, and she gives little thought to families for whom a bargain is not a temptation but a necessity. It would have been fairer to recommend that consumers be encouraged to buy less and better, rather than to buy nothing. The final chapters, moreover, repeat points already made.

Even so, the book is persuasive where it matters most. It does not ask us to feel guilty; it asks us to notice. I would suggest that anyone who has ever regretted an impulse buy read it before the next sale. Three and a half stars out of five.

8.title: Complaint about a misleading advertisement
8.brief: Write a formal letter to an advertising standards authority complaining about a campaign aimed at children that gives a misleading impression of a product. Explain the problem and say what you want the authority to do.
8.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal a una autoridad de publicidad quejándote de una campaña dirigida a niños que engaña sobre un producto.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Sir or Madam, a clear complaint in the opening sentence, enclosures and Yours faithfully.
At least three subjunctive structures (ask that… investigate, that… be required, It is important that… not suggest).
Direct and indirect objects in both patterns (send me a copy / explain them to parents) and the expression “target audience”.
8.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to submit a formal complaint about an advertising campaign for a fruit drink called Vita Kids, which is currently being broadcast on television and displayed on buses throughout the city.

The advertisements, whose target audience is clearly children, present the drink as a healthy source of vitamins and show a cartoon character handing it to smiling pupils. However, the label reveals that a single bottle contains more than six teaspoons of sugar. I believe that this gives parents a misleading impression and offers children a product that is anything but healthy. Having bought the drink myself for my nephews, I felt that I had been sold something under false pretences.

I therefore ask that the authority investigate the campaign and that the company be required to withdraw any claim that cannot be substantiated. It is also important that advertisements aimed at children not suggest that sugary drinks are part of a balanced diet. I would be grateful if you could send me a copy of your guidelines on this subject, so that I can explain them to other parents in my school community.

I enclose photographs of the label and of two of the advertisements. I am willing to supply any further evidence you may require. Unless these practices are challenged, companies will keep targeting a young audience with messages that parents cannot easily counter.

Thank you for your attention. I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Adriana Salcedo

8.title: The case for a cooling-off period online
8.brief: Write an opinion article arguing that online shops should be required to give customers a cooling-off period after a purchase. Begin with a personal anecdote and answer the objections of retailers.
8.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de opinión que defienda un período de reflexión obligatorio tras las compras en línea. Empieza con una anécdota y responde a las objeciones de los comercios.
criteria: At least two subjunctive structures (propose that… be required, It is vital that… be easy to use).
Direct and indirect objects in both patterns (offer customers a period / bring the decision to us).
At least three expressions from the unit (impulse buy, to drive up, brand loyalty) and a closing sentence that returns to the opening anecdote.
8.model:
It is eleven at night. I am tired, slightly bored and scrolling through my phone when an advertisement shows me a pair of boots at half price, with a timer counting down from ten minutes. Three clicks later, the boots are mine. By morning, I have forgotten why I wanted them.

Online shops have spent years perfecting the art of the impulse buy. Countdown clocks, 'only two left' warnings and one-click payment are designed to bring the decision to us before we have time to think. They are so effective that many of us now buy things we would never have bought in a shop, where the effort of walking to the till gives us time to reconsider.

I therefore propose that every online retailer be required to offer customers a cooling-off period of twenty-four hours, during which an order could be cancelled without penalty. Some countries already grant consumers a right to withdraw from distance purchases, but few shops advertise it. It is vital that the right be easy to use, and that the shop send buyers a clear reminder of it by email.

Retailers will object that such a rule would drive up their costs and create paperwork. But a business that depends on customers who buy without thinking is, in the long run, building brand loyalty on sand. A shopper who keeps a purchase after reflection is far more likely to return than one who sends it back a fortnight later.

As for the boots, I sent them back. The law gave me the time to change my mind; it should give everyone the same chance.

9.title: Should we bring back extinct species?
9.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether scientists should use genetic technology to bring extinct species back to life.
9.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si los científicos deberían revivir especies extintas con tecnología genética.
criteria: Two noun clauses with whoever / whatever (Whatever the benefits, …).
One contrast between whenever / wherever and when / where.
Use “biodiversity”, “ecosystem” and “to be on the brink of”.
9.model:
In 2025, a biotechnology company announced that it had created mice with the woolly coat of a mammoth, and that it intended to bring the mammoth itself back to life within a decade. "De-extinction", once the stuff of science fiction, is now a serious scientific project. But should it be?

Supporters argue that reviving lost species could restore damaged ecosystems. Mammoths, for example, once trampled the Arctic snow and kept the permafrost frozen; their return might slow the release of greenhouse gases. Whoever has seen a museum skeleton of a dodo can understand the emotional appeal of undoing humanity's past mistakes. Moreover, the techniques developed could help species that are on the brink of extinction today, by increasing their genetic diversity.

Opponents, however, raise powerful objections. Whatever the scientific achievement, a single cloned animal is not a species: it has no parents to learn from and no habitat that still exists in its original form. Wherever such creatures were released, they could behave unpredictably and threaten the animals that live there now. Perhaps the strongest argument is economic. The millions spent on de-extinction could protect thousands of hectares of rainforest, where biodiversity is being lost every day.

In my opinion, the research should continue, but only as a tool for conservation, not as a spectacle. When a species disappears, the real lesson is that prevention is far cheaper than resurrection. Whoever controls this technology must remember that the best way to save an animal is not to lose it in the first place.

9.title: A proposal for protecting a local habitat
9.brief: Write a proposal to your local council or an environmental fund for a project to protect a habitat in your region (a wetland, a river, a forest).
9.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al concejo local o a un fondo ambiental para proteger un hábitat de tu región.
criteria: Headings: Background, Objectives, Proposed actions, Budget, Expected outcomes.
One noun clause with whoever or whatever and one clause with whenever / wherever.
Use “habitat”, “to encroach on” and “resilience”.
9.model:
Proposal: Restoring the Juan Amarillo Wetland

Background
The Juan Amarillo wetland in north-west Bogotá is home to more than 100 species of birds, including the endemic Bogotá rail. Over the past thirty years, however, housing developments have encroached on the wetland, reducing its area by almost 40%. Pollution from illegal waste dumping and untreated sewage threatens what remains.

Objectives
The project aims to restore the wetland's natural habitat, improve water quality and involve local residents in its long-term protection.

Proposed actions
1. Planting 5,000 native trees and aquatic plants along the edges of the wetland to strengthen the ecosystem's resilience.
2. Installing filters at the three main points where wastewater enters.
3. Creating a volunteer "guardians" programme. Whoever joins will receive training in bird monitoring and environmental education.
4. Placing information boards and bins wherever visitors gather, and organising monthly clean-up days.

Budget
We request COP 180 million over two years, of which 60% would be allocated to restoration work, 25% to water treatment and 15% to community activities.

Expected outcomes
Within two years, we expect a measurable increase in bird populations and a significant reduction in waste. Whatever the final figures, the programme will have created a network of residents committed to the wetland's future, which is perhaps its most lasting benefit.

Conclusion
Wetlands are among the most valuable — and most threatened — ecosystems in the city. Protecting Juan Amarillo now will cost far less than restoring it later.

9.title: An encounter with wildlife
9.brief: Write a narrative for a nature magazine about a memorable encounter with an animal in the wild, and reflect on what it taught you about conservation.
9.briefEs: Escribe una narración para una revista de naturaleza sobre un encuentro memorable con un animal salvaje.
criteria: One clause with whenever or wherever and one noun clause with whatever.
Vivid descriptive language and a reflective ending.
Use “endangered”, “to poach” or “conservation”.
9.model:
We had been sitting in the canoe for almost two hours, in the middle of a black-water lagoon near Puerto Nariño, when our guide, Don Ismael, raised his hand. "Listen," he whispered.

At first, I heard nothing but insects. Then came a soft, explosive breath, like a sigh from beneath the water. A few metres away, a pink shape rose to the surface, curved gracefully and disappeared again. Then another. Within minutes, we were surrounded by a family of Amazon river dolphins.

I had seen photographs, of course, but nothing prepared me for the colour — a rosy pink that seemed impossible in nature — or for their curiosity. One young dolphin swam directly under the canoe, turned on its side and appeared to look at us. Whatever it was thinking, I felt, for a moment, that we were the ones being observed.

On the way back, Don Ismael told us that the species is now endangered. Fishermen used to kill them to use as bait, and poaching continues in some areas. Dams and mercury from illegal gold mining are poisoning the rivers. "Wherever there is mining," he said, "the dolphins disappear."

I think about that afternoon whenever I read about the Amazon. Conservation can sound like an abstract word, full of statistics and policies. For me, it now has a face — pink, curious and, for the moment, still breathing.

9.title: Should tourism in national parks be limited?
9.brief: Write an academic essay on whether the number of visitors to national parks should be limited to protect fragile ecosystems. Weigh the benefits of tourism against its costs.
9.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico sobre si se debe limitar el número de visitantes a los parques nacionales para proteger ecosistemas frágiles.
criteria: At least four -ever words (wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever, however) used correctly, including one noun clause with whoever or whatever.
At least one when or where clause for a specific time or place, contrasted with an -ever clause.
At least three expressions from the unit (ecosystem, habitat, conservation, to be on the brink of, resilience).
9.model:
National parks exist to protect nature, yet they also attract millions of visitors whose presence can damage the ecosystems they come to admire. Should the number of tourists be limited? This essay argues that, in the most fragile areas, it should.

Tourism brings undeniable benefits. Wherever a park is well managed, it generates income for local communities and gives governments a reason to preserve habitats that might otherwise be converted to farmland. Visitors who experience nature directly often become advocates for conservation. Whoever has watched a whale surface beside a boat is unlikely to forget the experience, or to support its destruction.

However, the costs are equally real. Footpaths erode, wildlife is disturbed and waste accumulates, particularly when visitors arrive in large groups. Some reefs are said to be on the brink of collapse because of boats, anchors and sunscreen. Whenever numbers exceed what an area can absorb, its resilience declines, and whatever income the park earns in the short term is lost in the long term.
