A system of daily quotas, reviewed annually by scientists, would offer a practical compromise. However popular a destination may be, it can only receive as many people as its ecosystem tolerates. Prices could be raised in peak season, with the revenue invested in conservation. Wherever quotas are introduced, visitors will need time to adjust, but most are likely to accept them if the reasons are explained. Parks are not theme parks: their purpose is to keep nature alive, not merely to entertain whoever happens to turn up.

9.title: Executive summary: planting trees in the city
9.brief: Write the executive summary of a report on a city tree-planting programme. State the purpose, the main findings and your recommendations, and propose next steps.
9.briefEs: Escribe el resumen ejecutivo de un informe sobre un programa de siembra de árboles en la ciudad, con hallazgos, recomendaciones y próximos pasos.
criteria: Headings: Purpose, Findings, Recommendations and Next steps.
At least four -ever words (wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever, however) used correctly.
At least one when or where clause for a specific time or place and at least two expressions from the unit (biodiversity, resilience, habitat, ecosystem).
9.model:
Executive Summary: Planting Trees in the City

Purpose
This summary outlines the results of a two-year programme in which volunteers planted 1,200 native trees in the city of Cali, and recommends whether it should be extended. It is intended for the city council.

Findings
Wherever trees were planted along main roads, temperatures at street level fell by up to three degrees on hot afternoons. Birds returned to several districts where they had not been seen for years, and residents reported that they now sit outside whenever the weather allows. However successful the planting was, survival rates varied: 82 per cent of trees survived in neighbourhoods where residents watered them regularly, compared with only 51 per cent where nobody took responsibility. Whoever looked after the trees determined whether they survived. The cost was modest, at roughly COP 60,000 per tree.

Recommendations
We recommend that the programme be extended to six more districts over the next two years. Whatever funding is approved should include a maintenance budget, because planting without care is a waste of money. Each new site should be assigned to a named group of residents, who would be trained and supported by the municipal gardening team. Whenever a tree dies, it should be replaced within one season.

Next steps
A progress report should be presented to the council in twelve months. If the survival rate of new trees reaches 80 per cent, the programme could be considered a lasting contribution to the city's biodiversity and resilience to heat.

9.title: Protecting sea turtle nests on our beach
9.brief: Write a proposal to a regional environmental fund for a community project that protects sea turtle nests on a local beach. Describe the problem, the actions, the budget and the expected results.
9.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a un fondo ambiental regional para un proyecto comunitario que proteja los nidos de tortugas marinas en una playa local.
criteria: Headings: Background, Proposed actions, Budget and Expected outcomes.
At least four -ever words (wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever, however), including one noun clause with whoever or whatever.
At least two when or where clauses for specific times or places and at least two expressions from the unit (endangered, poacher, habitat, conservation).
9.model:
Proposal: Protecting Sea Turtle Nests on Our Beach

Background
Every year, sea turtles come ashore on the beaches near our village to lay their eggs, and several of the species that do so are endangered. Wherever people and nests share a beach, the eggs are at risk: they are trampled by visitors, disturbed by dogs and, in some places, taken by poachers who sell them as food. Local fishermen estimate that fewer than half of the nests now hatch successfully.

Proposed actions
The project would have four components. First, we would recruit twenty local volunteers to patrol the beach at night during the nesting season, whenever the tide allows turtles to come ashore. Second, each nest would be marked with a protective cage, wherever it is found, so that visitors can see where not to walk. Third, we would offer a short training course to whoever wishes to volunteer, so that nests are moved only when the sea threatens them. Finally, we would run an awareness campaign in schools and hotels, explaining that dogs must be kept on leads and that lights must be switched off after dark.

Budget
The total cost for the first season is COP 14,000,000, mostly for cages, torches and training materials. Volunteers would receive a small food allowance, and the municipality has offered to lend us a storage hut.

Expected outcomes
Whatever the exact figures, we expect the proportion of nests that hatch to rise substantially within three years. Protecting the beach would also preserve a habitat on which many other species depend, and it would give the village a source of pride and, eventually, ecotourism income.

9.title: Review: a documentary series on a wetland
9.brief: Write a critical review of a nature documentary, real or imagined. Evaluate the images, the narration and the message, and say who should watch it.
9.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de un documental de naturaleza, real o imaginado: imágenes, narración y mensaje.
criteria: At least three -ever words (wherever, whoever, whatever, however, whenever) used correctly.
At least two expressions from the unit (ecosystem, habitat, conservation).
Balanced evaluation with one strength, one weakness and a final rating.
9.model:
The Last Wetland, a three-part documentary series now streaming, follows a year in the life of a marsh in the Colombian Orinoquía, one of the richest and least known ecosystems in South America. Filmed by a small local crew over eighteen months, it asks what will happen to the animals that depend on the marsh as the dry seasons grow longer.

Its greatest achievement is access. Wherever the crew went, the camera seems to have been welcome, and the footage of a giant anteater crossing flooded grassland at dawn is unforgettable. Whoever is responsible for the sound design deserves special praise: the calls of howler monkeys and the hum of insects create an atmosphere so rich that one almost feels the humidity. The series also gives a voice to local ranchers, who explain how they manage their land so that cattle and wildlife can share it.

Unfortunately, the narration is the weak point. However striking the images, the commentary repeatedly resorts to clichés, and the final episode becomes a lecture in which whatever the viewer has just seen is explained a second time. The warnings about climate change, important as they are, would have had more force if the film had trusted its pictures.

Even so, The Last Wetland is a valuable piece of conservation filmmaking. Whoever watches it will understand why this landscape deserves protection. Three and a half stars out of five, and an easy recommendation for families.

9.title: Illegal dumping in our stream
9.brief: Write a formal letter to the regional environmental authority asking it to act against illegal dumping in a stream near your home. Describe the damage and say what you want the authority to do.
9.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal a la autoridad ambiental regional pidiendo que actúe contra el vertido ilegal de basura en una quebrada cerca de tu casa.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Sir or Madam, a clear request in the opening sentence, enclosures and Yours faithfully.
At least four -ever words (wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever, however) used correctly.
At least one when or where clause for a specific time or place and at least two expressions from the unit (biodiversity, to encroach on, habitat).
9.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing on behalf of the residents' association of La Esperanza to ask that your authority inspect illegal dumping along the stream that runs through our neighbourhood.

For at least two years, rubble, old furniture and household waste have been left on the banks, usually at night. Wherever the path is wide enough for a lorry, there are now mounds of rubbish, and whenever it rains, a good part of it is washed into the water. The stream, where children used to catch fish, is now almost lifeless. Whoever is responsible is clearly not afraid of being caught, since we have never seen a patrol.

The consequences extend beyond appearance. The pollution threatens the biodiversity of the area, which includes several bird species that nest in the reeds, and the rubbish has already begun to encroach on the small community garden at the water's edge. However much the municipality spends on cleaning, the problem will return unless the source is dealt with. Whatever measures you decide to take, we ask that residents be consulted before they are implemented.

We therefore request three things: an inspection of the site within the next month, the installation of a camera or regular patrols at the three main access points, and a public meeting at which we can present our evidence. I enclose photographs and a list of dates on which dumping was observed. Volunteers from our association are willing to help with a clean-up day whenever your staff are available.

Thank you for your attention. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Hernán Duarte
Residents' Association of La Esperanza

9.title: A small pond and a big idea
9.brief: Write a speech for a school assembly on Earth Day. Use one small local place as an example of why conservation matters, and challenge your audience to act.
9.briefEs: Escribe un discurso para una asamblea escolar del Día de la Tierra: usa un pequeño lugar local para mostrar por qué importa la conservación y rétalos a actuar.
criteria: At least four -ever words (wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever, however) used correctly.
At least two when or where clauses for specific times or places, contrasted with -ever clauses.
At least three expressions from the unit (habitat, ecosystem, conservation, endangered) and a spoken register with a clear challenge to the audience.
9.model:
Good morning, everyone. Today I would like to talk about a place that is only twenty metres wide: the pond behind our science block.

Most of you have walked past it a thousand times. Some of you may have eaten your lunch beside it without noticing the life around you. Whenever it rains, it fills up, and whenever it is dry, it shrinks to a muddy puddle. Yet in that small space live dragonflies, frogs and, last spring, a family of ducks. That pond is a habitat, and for those animals it is the whole world.

Whoever thinks that conservation is only about pandas and rainforests is mistaken. Whatever the size of a place, its ecosystem depends on balance. When one thing disappears, others follow. Last year, when the pond was drained for repairs, the frogs vanished for months. Where there was life, there was silence.

However small our contribution may seem, it matters. Wherever you are, you can plant native flowers, avoid dropping litter and speak up when something looks wrong. Even a small garden can shelter dozens of species. You do not need to be a scientist to protect a place that you love.

So here is my challenge. For one week, notice one living thing on your way to school. Learn its name. Find out whether it is common or endangered. I promise that, whoever you are, you will never walk past it in the same way again.

Thank you, and happy Earth Day.

10.title: Should English be the global language of science?
10.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether it is beneficial or harmful that most scientific research is published in English.
10.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si es positivo o negativo que casi toda la ciencia se publique en inglés.
criteria: A range of passive forms (is published, has been argued, being judged, to be translated).
Correct subject-verb agreement with quantifiers (each of, none of, a number of, the majority of).
Use “mother tongue”, “to get your point across” and “lost in translation”.
10.model:
It has been estimated that more than 90% of articles in the natural sciences are now published in English. For researchers in Colombia, Brazil or China, mastering a foreign language is therefore no longer optional. Is this dominance a benefit or a barrier?

The advantages are clear. A common language allows ideas to be shared across borders instantly. When a vaccine is being developed or a new species is discovered, the findings can be read by scientists everywhere. A number of major breakthroughs have resulted from international collaborations that would have been impossible without a lingua franca.

However, the costs are significant and often overlooked. Researchers whose mother tongue is not English must spend years — and considerable money — learning to write academic prose. Each of these scientists is competing with native speakers who can get their point across with far less effort, and studies show that non-native authors' papers are more likely to be rejected for "language problems". Valuable local knowledge is also being lost: research on Colombian ecosystems or indigenous medicine is sometimes ignored simply because it was published in Spanish. Nuance, too, can be lost in translation.

None of this means that English should be abandoned. The majority of scientists agree that a shared language is indispensable. Yet the system could be made fairer. Journals could accept submissions in several languages and have them translated using AI tools, and editors could be trained to judge papers on their ideas rather than their style. Science, after all, should be measured by what it discovers, not by how fluently it is written.

10.title: Slang, dialects and identity
10.brief: Write an article for a language-learning website about the role of slang and regional dialects in Colombia and what they reveal about identity.
10.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre el papel de la jerga y los dialectos regionales en Colombia y lo que revelan sobre la identidad.
criteria: Agreement with quantifiers and collective nouns (everyone, most of the vocabulary, a lot of words).
Three passive constructions.
Use “dialect”, “slang” and “loan word”.
10.model:
Parce, Bacano, Chévere: What Colombian Slang Says About Us

For a country of 52 million people, Colombia has a remarkable variety of ways of speaking. Every region has its own dialect, and almost everyone can identify where a speaker comes from within a few words.

In Medellín, friends are called "parce" — a shortened form of "parcero", which is thought to have come from the word "parcela", or plot of land. In Bogotá, something excellent is "chévere" or "bacano", while on the Caribbean coast, it might be "nítido". People from Cali are known for "ve" and "mirá", which show the influence of the "voseo", a form of address that most of the country abandoned centuries ago.

Much of this vocabulary has been shaped by history. A lot of words in Colombian slang are loan words from English, such as "man" or "parche" (from "patch"), while others come from indigenous languages: "chusco" (attractive) is believed to derive from Quechua. Some expressions were popularised by television series and are now used by speakers who have never been to the regions they come from.

Slang is often dismissed as "bad Spanish", but linguists disagree. Each dialect has its own consistent grammar and sound system. More importantly, the way we speak is a badge of identity. None of the students I teach abroad sounds more "Colombian" than when they slip into regional slang with a friend.

For learners of Spanish, my advice is simple: learn the standard forms, but don't ignore the slang. That is where a language really comes alive.

10.title: How I finally got my tongue around English sounds
10.brief: Write a reflective piece about a specific difficulty you have had with English (pronunciation, phrasal verbs, idioms) and how you have dealt with it.
10.briefEs: Escribe un texto reflexivo sobre una dificultad concreta con el inglés y cómo la has enfrentado.
criteria: Passive forms in at least three different tenses.
Two quantifier subjects with correct agreement (Neither of…, Every one of…).
Use “to get your tongue around”, “to pick up” and “fluent”.
10.model:
For years, there was one sound in English that I simply could not get my tongue around: the "th" in words like "think" and "this". Spanish speakers in Colombia are not used to placing the tongue between the teeth, and every time I tried, I felt ridiculous.

At school, pronunciation was barely taught. We were given lists of vocabulary to memorise and grammar exercises to complete, but none of the lessons was devoted to sounds. As a result, I said "I tink" and "dis" well into my twenties, and I was often misunderstood. Once, at a conference in Toronto, I told a colleague I was "sinking" about his proposal. Neither of us knew where to look.

What changed things was a decision to be recorded. A tutor I found online asked me to read short texts aloud, and every recording was played back with the problem sounds highlighted. Hearing myself was painful, but it worked. I also picked up a trick from a YouTube channel: exaggerating the sound in front of a mirror until it no longer felt strange.

I would not call myself perfectly fluent, and every one of my friends from abroad can still hear my accent. But I no longer feel anxious when I have to say "three thousand". The sound that was once avoided at all costs has been tamed.

The lesson, I think, is that pronunciation is a physical skill, not an intellectual one. It cannot be learned from a book; it has to be practised, repeatedly, out loud.

10.title: Immersion or classroom: which works better?
10.brief: Write an academic essay comparing language learning through immersion abroad with learning in a classroom. Weigh the arguments and reach a reasoned conclusion.
10.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico que compare aprender un idioma por inmersión en el extranjero con aprenderlo en el aula.
criteria: At least four passive forms in different tenses or with modals (is taught, have been taught, can be explained, must be…), including one get-passive (get invited).
At least three quantifier subjects with correct agreement (A number of… are, Each of… must, None of… is, The majority of… are).
At least two expressions from the unit (to pick up, to get your point across, fluent, mother tongue).
10.model:
It is often said that languages are best learned by living in a country where they are spoken. Total immersion, it is claimed, forces learners to pick up vocabulary and grammar naturally. Yet millions of people have been taught English successfully in classrooms. Which approach is more effective?

The case for immersion is strong. A learner who is surrounded by the language every day is constantly being exposed to authentic speech, and mistakes are corrected naturally by conversation. A number of studies suggest that students who spend a year abroad make faster progress in speaking than those who remain at home. Moreover, each of these learners must get their point across in real situations, which builds confidence.

However, immersion is not available to everyone, and it is not always effective. Learners who live among compatriots abroad may never be forced to use the language, and none of the advice given by well-meaning locals is guaranteed to be accurate. By contrast, a good classroom provides structure. Grammar can be explained, errors can be analysed, and progress can be measured. A great deal of the progress made by intermediate learners depends on precisely this kind of guidance.

The best approach is probably a combination. Learners who have been given a solid foundation in class tend to benefit far more from time abroad, and those who get invited to join local activities progress fastest of all. Neither method is sufficient alone, and nothing can replace regular practice. In the end, what matters is not where a language is learned, but how often it is used.

10.title: Report: English in local businesses
10.brief: Write a report on a survey of local businesses about their use of English and the skills they expect from employees. Present the findings and recommend improvements.
10.briefEs: Escribe un informe sobre una encuesta a empresas locales acerca de su uso del inglés y las habilidades que esperan de sus empleados.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
At least four passive forms in different tenses or with modals (is used, were caused, have been trained, should be designed), including one get-passive (get sent).
At least three quantifier subjects with correct agreement (The majority of… reported, Each of… had, None of… was) and two expressions from the unit (fluent, lost in translation).
10.model:
Report: English in Local Businesses

Introduction
This report presents the results of a survey in which forty small and medium-sized businesses in Medellín were asked about their use of English. The aim was to identify the language skills which are most needed in the local workplace.

Findings
The majority of companies reported that English is used at least weekly, mainly for emails and video calls. A number of employers said that applicants are rarely tested on speaking, even though a lot of daily communication is spoken. Each of the three largest firms had experienced misunderstandings that were caused by poor pronunciation or by expressions that were lost in translation. None of the companies surveyed was satisfied with the English level of new graduates. Employees who are promoted to management are expected to be fluent, yet only half of them have been trained in business English. A few respondents mentioned that staff get sent on courses which are too general to be useful.

Recommendations
It is recommended that speaking skills be assessed during recruitment, and that training be tailored to the needs of each department. Courses should be designed with the help of employers, so that the vocabulary taught is genuinely used. Staff should also be encouraged to practise through conversation exchanges, where a native speaker can be met informally. These measures would cost relatively little and could be introduced gradually.

Conclusion
English is clearly valued by local employers, but the skills that graduates are given do not yet match what is required.

10.title: A language exchange programme for our university
10.brief: Write a proposal to the international office of your university for a language exchange programme that pairs local and international students. Explain the need, the plan, the resources and the expected results.
10.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a la oficina internacional de tu universidad para un programa de intercambio de idiomas que empareje estudiantes locales e internacionales.
criteria: Headings: Background, Proposal, Resources and Expected results.
At least four passive forms in different tenses or with modals (are paired, would be appointed, can be set up, will be regarded).
At least three quantifier subjects with correct agreement (A great deal of… is, The majority of… could, Each of… would, None of… is) and two expressions from the unit (mother tongue, to pick up).
10.model:
Proposal: A Language Exchange Programme for Our University

Background
International students are often found sitting alone in the cafeteria, while local students who want to practise English or French rarely meet them. A great deal of potential learning is therefore wasted. A number of universities have shown that structured language exchanges can be set up easily, and that they are valued by both sides.

Proposal
We propose a language exchange programme in which each local student is paired with an international student for a semester. Every pair would meet for one hour a week, speaking half the time in each partner's mother tongue. Participants would be asked to keep a short diary of new words they have picked up, and a coordinator would be appointed to resolve problems. The majority of meetings could take place in the cafeteria, but some would be walking tours of the city, so that pairs get to know it together. Each of the pairs would receive a list of conversation topics, so that nobody is left without anything to say.

Resources
The programme requires only a part-time coordinator, whose salary would be paid by the international office, and a modest budget for materials and refreshments, estimated at COP 2,000,000 per semester. None of these costs is significant for a university of our size.

Expected results
We expect every participant to gain confidence in speaking, and a lot of friendships are likely to be formed. Students who might otherwise never get invited to a local home may find themselves welcomed by a family. Our hope is that the number of participants will have doubled within two years.

10.title: Review: an app for learners of English
10.brief: Write a critical review of a language-learning app, real or imagined. Evaluate its method, its strengths and weaknesses, and say who it is suitable for.
10.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de una aplicación para aprender idiomas, real o imaginada: método, fortalezas, debilidades y a quién le conviene.
criteria: At least four passive forms in different tenses or with modals (is introduced, have been recorded, is charged, are presented), including one get-passive (get reminded).
At least three quantifier subjects with correct agreement (Each of… is, A lot of… use, None of… requires, A number of… are, The majority of… would).
At least three expressions from the unit (to pick up, to get your point across, lost in translation, fluent) and a final rating.
10.model:
LinguaLoop, a new app for learners of English, promises that users will be speaking fluently in six months. That is a bold claim, and it deserves to be tested. I used the app for eight weeks, at least twenty minutes a day.

The app has real strengths. The interface is clean, and new users are guided through the first lesson step by step. Each of the lessons is short, and the vocabulary is introduced through images and audio rather than translation, so that words are picked up in context. A lot of the exercises use natural recordings of regional accents, which is rare for apps of this kind. Progress is tracked clearly, and learners get reminded to review words just before they would forget them.

Unfortunately, the app has weaknesses too. Speaking practice, which is the skill most learners want to improve, is limited to repeating sentences that have been recorded in advance. None of the exercises requires users to get their point across in a real conversation, and the feedback on pronunciation is so general that it is almost useless. A number of expressions are presented without context, so that idioms are easily lost in translation. The subscription, which is charged annually, is also expensive.

In short, LinguaLoop is a useful supplement, but it will not make anyone fluent on its own. The majority of its users would be better served by combining it with conversation practice. Two and a half stars out of five.

10.title: Application for a language scholarship
10.brief: Write a formal letter applying for a scholarship to attend a short English course abroad. Explain your learning history, your difficulties and why you deserve the award.
10.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal postulándote a una beca para un curso corto de inglés en el extranjero: tu historia como estudiante, tus dificultades y por qué la mereces.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Members of the Selection Committee, a clear purpose in the opening sentence, a polite closing and Yours faithfully.
At least four passive forms in different tenses or with modals (is offered, were taught, was told, cannot be learned, has been put).

At least three quantifier subjects with correct agreement (Most of… were, A number of… admitted, Each of… has shown, None of… has) and two expressions from the unit (to get your point across, fluent, to pick up).
10.model:
Dear Members of the Selection Committee,

I am writing to apply for the language scholarship that is offered each year by the Fundación Horizonte for a four-week English course in Edinburgh.

I have studied English since the age of eight. Most of my classes were taught in large groups, and a number of my teachers admitted that speaking practice was neglected. As a result, I can read academic texts without difficulty, yet I still struggle to get my point across in conversation. Each of my attempts to speak with foreign visitors at the tourist office, where I volunteer, has shown me how much I still have to learn. Last summer, I was told by a visitor from Scotland that I was 'very clear but very formal', an observation I have never forgotten.

I believe that the course would be of great value to me. I am studying tourism, and the majority of jobs in my field require fluent English. I would also like to pick up the way everyday English is used, something which cannot be learned from books. If I were awarded the scholarship, I would be expected to complete weekly assessments, and I would gladly accept this requirement.

None of my family has ever travelled abroad, and the cost of the course is far beyond our means. A great deal of effort has been put into my education by my parents, and I wish to repay it. I would be honoured to represent the foundation and to share what I have learned with other students on my return.

Thank you for considering my application.

Yours faithfully,
Daniela Quintero

10.title: Stop apologising for your accent
10.brief: Write an opinion article arguing that language learners should not apologise for their accent. Begin with an observation from everyday life, make your case and end with advice.
10.briefEs: Escribe un artículo de opinión defendiendo que quienes aprenden idiomas no deben disculparse por su acento. Empieza con una observación cotidiana y termina con un consejo.
criteria: At least four passive forms in different tenses or with modals (are followed, was spoken, can be lost, cannot be taught), including one get-passive (gets interrupted).
At least three quantifier or negative subjects with correct agreement (Most… are, The majority of… take place, None of… does, Each of… has).
At least three expressions from the unit (mother tongue, to pick up, to get your point across) and a final piece of advice to the reader.
10.model:
'Sorry for my English.' I have heard these words, and said them, more times than I can count. Every time, they are followed by a small laugh, as if having an accent were a social error. I believe that it is time we stopped apologising.

An accent is not a mistake. It is the sound of a person's history: the mother tongue that was spoken at home, the town where they grew up and the other languages which they have picked up on the way. Most speakers of English in the world today are not native speakers, and the majority of conversations in English take place between people for whom it is a second or third language. In such a context, the aim is not to sound like someone else but to be understood.

None of this means that clarity does not matter. But there is a difference between being understood and being corrected into sounding like a stereotype. Each of us has met people who are mocked for the way they speak, and each of us has seen how quickly confidence can be lost. A learner who is laughed at, or who gets interrupted every time a vowel is mispronounced, will soon say nothing.

So the next time you are tempted to apologise, try something different. Say what you want to say, and let the listener do their share of the work. After all, getting your point across is not a matter of perfect sounds. It is a matter of courage, and that cannot be taught.

11.title: Are role models still necessary?
11.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether young people need role models, and whether celebrities and influencers are suitable ones.
11.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si los jóvenes necesitan modelos a seguir y si las celebridades lo son.
criteria: Four compound adjectives (self-taught, world-famous, hard-working, well-known).
One superlative compound adjective (the best-known, the most widely read).
Use “role model”, “to look up to” and “to leave a legacy”.
11.model:
Young people today are surrounded by potential role models. With a few clicks, they can follow world-famous athletes, award-winning scientists and influencers with millions of followers. But do they really need someone to look up to — and, if so, are these the right people?

There is good evidence that role models matter. Children who see someone like them succeed are more likely to believe they can do the same. When Colombian cyclist Egan Bernal won the Tour de France in 2019, cycling clubs across the country reported a surge in young members. Role models can show that success is possible, especially for children from disadvantaged backgrounds, who may have few examples of hard-working professionals around them.

The problem lies in who young people choose. The best-known figures on social media are often famous for their lifestyle rather than their achievements. Their carefully edited, picture-perfect lives can create unrealistic expectations and encourage materialism. Moreover, celebrities are human, and when a well-respected star is involved in a scandal, the disappointment for young fans can be profound.

In my opinion, role models remain valuable, but they need not be famous. Some of the most inspiring examples are found closer to home: a self-taught grandmother who started a business, a teacher who never gave up on difficult students. Such people may not trend on social media, but they leave a legacy that lasts far longer than any viral video. Rather than banning influencers, schools should help young people think critically about the people they choose to admire.

11.title: Nomination for an award
11.brief: Write a letter nominating someone you know for a community award for exceptional people. Describe their achievements and why they deserve recognition.
11.briefEs: Escribe una carta nominando a alguien que conoces a un premio comunitario para personas excepcionales.
criteria: Five compound adjectives, including one superlative compound (the hardest-working, the most far-reaching).
Formal letter structure with a clear recommendation.
Use “against all odds”, “resilient” and “groundbreaking”.
11.model:
Dear Members of the Selection Committee,

I am writing to nominate Doña Rosalba Mosquera for the 2026 Community Hero Award. I have known her for eight years as a neighbour and fellow volunteer, and I can think of no one who deserves this recognition more.

Doña Rosalba, a sixty-two-year-old retired cleaner from Quibdó, arrived in Bogotá in 2001 after being displaced by violence. Against all odds, she rebuilt her life in a city where she knew no one. Ten years ago, she noticed that many children in the neighbourhood were spending their afternoons alone on the streets while their parents worked. With no money and no official support, she opened her own home as an after-school space.

What began as a handful of children doing homework at her kitchen table has grown into a well-organised community centre that serves more than 120 children every week. Her approach was groundbreaking for the area: alongside homework help, she introduced traditional Pacific music and dance classes, which have given many young people a sense of pride in their roots. Several of her former students are now at university.

Doña Rosalba is the hardest-working, most big-hearted person I know. She is resilient but humble, and she always insists that the credit belongs to the volunteers. Her impact on our community has been among the most far-reaching I have witnessed.

I hope you will consider her nomination. I would be happy to provide further information or testimonies from families.

Yours faithfully,
Julián Arango

11.title: Profile: a trailblazer in your field
11.brief: Write a profile of a person who blazed a trail in a field you are interested in (science, sport, art, business), for a website celebrating exceptional people.
11.briefEs: Escribe un perfil de una persona pionera en un campo que te interese para un sitio web sobre personas excepcionales.
criteria: Five compound adjectives, including two before nouns (a record-breaking career).
One superlative compound adjective.
Use “to blaze a trail”, “to overcome” and “determined”.
11.model:
Francisca Ramírez: The Scientist Who Mapped the Invisible

Few people outside the scientific world have heard of Dr. Francisca Ramírez, yet her work has changed the way we understand Colombia's rivers.

Born in a working-class family in Montería, she was the first person in her family to finish secondary school. Determined to study biology, she overcame enormous obstacles: she worked night shifts in a bakery to pay for her studies and taught herself English using second-hand textbooks. "I was largely self-taught," she recalls. "The library was my second home."

In the 1990s, when the study of freshwater microorganisms was considered a niche, low-prestige field, Ramírez blazed a trail. Her ground-breaking research showed that tiny, often invisible organisms could be used to measure the health of entire rivers — a cheap, reliable method that is now used across Latin America. Her long-term study of the Sinú river is one of the most widely cited environmental studies ever produced in the country.

Beyond her research, she has been a tireless, outspoken advocate for women in science. She founded a mentoring network that has supported more than 800 young female researchers from low-income backgrounds.

Now retired, Ramírez remains characteristically modest. When asked about her record-breaking career, she shrugs. "I simply asked questions that nobody else thought were important."

For a generation of Colombian scientists, she is proof that brilliance can come from anywhere — and that the most important discoveries are sometimes the ones nobody else is looking for.

11.title: Is success the result of talent or effort?
11.brief: Write an academic essay on whether success comes mainly from natural talent or from effort. Consider the role of opportunity and reach a balanced conclusion.
11.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo académico sobre si el éxito depende sobre todo del talento natural o del esfuerzo, considerando el papel de las oportunidades.
criteria: At least five compound adjectives (award-winning, hard-working, self-taught, long-lasting, well-meaning…).
At least one superlative compound adjective (the best-known, the most widely read).
At least two words from the unit (determined, resilient, against all odds, role model) and a balanced conclusion.
11.model:
Every award-winning athlete, scientist or artist is asked the same question: was it talent or hard work? The answer matters because it shapes how we educate children and how we judge ourselves. This essay argues that, while talent may open the door, effort determines what lies beyond it.

There is no doubt that natural ability exists. Some children learn languages with astonishing speed, and some young musicians seem to understand rhythm instinctively. The best-known prodigies, such as Mozart, are often cited as proof that greatness is innate. Yet historians note that Mozart's father was a demanding, full-time teacher who trained him intensively from the age of three.

In everyday life, effort matters even more. A hard-working student of average ability will usually outperform a gifted but complacent one over several years. Many self-taught programmers, for instance, have built long-lasting careers without any formal training, simply because they were determined to keep learning. Being resilient, which means continuing after failure, is arguably the most valuable single quality, and it can be developed by anyone.

Nevertheless, a belief in effort alone can be unfair. It suggests that those who fail did not try hard enough, ignoring the obstacles faced by children from poorer backgrounds. A well-meaning teacher who tells a pupil that 'anything is possible' may unintentionally make that pupil feel responsible for circumstances beyond their control. The fairest conclusion is that talent and effort are not rivals: the one needs the other, and both need opportunity. Societies that recognise this create more thoughtful, less judgemental classrooms.

11.title: Report: a mentoring scheme with former students
11.brief: Write a report evaluating the first year of a school mentoring scheme in which former students act as role models for current pupils. Present the findings and recommend changes.
11.briefEs: Escribe un informe que evalúe el primer año de un programa escolar de mentoría en el que exalumnos actúan como modelos para los estudiantes actuales.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
At least five compound adjectives (down-to-earth, self-taught, well-known, hands-on, short-term, up-to-date…) and at least one superlative compound (the most far-reaching).
At least two expressions from the unit (role model, to leave a legacy) in an objective, impersonal register.
11.model:
Report: A Mentoring Scheme with Former Students

Introduction
This report evaluates the first year of the school's mentoring scheme, in which twenty former students, now working in a variety of professions, acted as role models for pupils in their final two years.

Findings
Feedback was gathered from 90 pupils and all twenty mentors. Pupils described the mentors as down-to-earth and approachable, and many said that meeting someone who had come from the same neighbourhood made success seem more realistic. The most popular sessions were those led by self-taught entrepreneurs and by a well-known local journalist. Mentors, for their part, valued the opportunity to give something back, although several found the time commitment heavy. A small number of pupils, around 10 per cent, felt that their mentor was too busy or too distant to offer genuinely hands-on advice. The most far-reaching effect appears to have been on pupils' ambitions: the proportion who intended to apply for university rose from 48 to 63 per cent.

Recommendations
We recommend that the scheme continue for a second year, with some changes. Mentors should be asked to commit to a fixed, short-term schedule of six sessions, rather than an open-ended arrangement. Pupils who would benefit most from a high-achieving role model should be matched first, and the school should create a simple, up-to-date directory of mentors' areas of expertise. Finally, we suggest that some sessions be held online to include mentors who live far away.

Conclusion
The scheme has proved a cost-effective way of widening pupils' horizons. With modest adjustments, it could leave a legacy that lasts well beyond the school's walls.

11.title: Inspiring visitors: a speaker series for our school
11.brief: Write a proposal to the head teacher for a series of talks by inspiring local people. Explain the aim, the programme, the budget and the expected outcomes.
11.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a la directora para una serie de charlas con personas inspiradoras de la región: objetivo, programa, presupuesto y resultados esperados.
criteria: Headings: Aim, Programme, Budget and Expected outcomes.
At least five compound adjectives (well-respected, self-taught, long-serving, thought-provoking, world-famous…) and at least one superlative compound (the most widely admired).
At least two expressions from the unit (against all odds, to leave a legacy, to overcome, role model).
11.model:
Proposal: Inspiring Visitors, a Speaker Series for Our School

Aim
We propose a termly series of talks in which well-respected people from our region visit the school to describe how they overcame difficulties and built their careers. The aim is to show pupils that success can come from ordinary backgrounds.

Programme
Each talk would last forty-five minutes and would be followed by a question-and-answer session. Speakers would be selected from a wide range of fields: medicine, farming, sport, the arts and small business. We would give priority to people who have faced setbacks, such as a self-taught chef who started with a street stall or a long-serving nurse who completed her degree as a single parent. A thought-provoking talk by a speaker who made mistakes is, in our experience, more valuable than a polished presentation by a world-famous figure. The most widely admired speakers, we have found, are those who admit their failures.

Budget
The cost would be low. Speakers would be volunteers, and we would only need to cover transport, which we estimate at COP 150,000 per visit, and a small token of thanks. Twelve talks over the academic year would therefore cost approximately COP 1,800,000 in total.

Expected outcomes
We hope that pupils will leave each talk feeling that their own goals are within reach. Over time, the series could leave a lasting legacy: a bank of recorded interviews, which future classes could use, and a network of speakers willing to act as mentors. Against all odds, many of the people we have in mind achieved far more than anyone expected, and their stories deserve to be heard.

11.title: Review: a biography of a self-taught engineer
11.brief: Write a critical review of a biography, real or imagined, of someone who achieved a great deal in difficult circumstances. Evaluate how convincingly the book portrays the person.
11.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de una biografía, real o imaginada, de alguien que logró mucho en circunstancias difíciles.
criteria: At least five compound adjectives (self-taught, hard-working, well-researched, thought-provoking…) and at least one superlative compound (the best-loved, the best-known).
At least two expressions from the unit (against all odds, resilient, to leave a legacy).
Balanced evaluation with one strength, one weakness and a final rating.
11.model:
Bridges She Never Saw, a biography by Clara Montenegro, tells the story of Elisa Marín, a self-taught engineer who designed more than forty footbridges in remote villages of the Andes. Published last month, it runs to three hundred pages. Born in 1931 to a family of farm workers, Marín never attended university, yet her low-cost, earthquake-resistant designs became a model for rural communities.

Montenegro's greatest achievement is to make a modest, hard-working woman seem extraordinary without exaggeration. The scenes in which Marín, against all odds, persuades sceptical engineers to adopt her methods are gripping, and the descriptions of the mountains are lyrical. The book is also exceptionally well-researched: the author consulted letters, municipal records and interviews with more than thirty villagers, giving the story a warmth that official histories lack.

Where the book disappoints is in its uncritical admiration. Marín is presented as the most selfless, the most patient and the best-loved person in every village she visited, and the portrait begins to feel one-dimensional. Her failures, including a bridge that collapsed in 1978, are mentioned briefly and then forgotten. A more balanced account would have shown a resilient but imperfect woman, and would have made her achievements seem even more impressive.

Even so, this is a moving, thought-provoking biography that deserves a wide readership. It reminds us that the people who leave the most lasting legacy are not always the best-known. Four stars out of five.

11.title: A reference for a former student
11.brief: Write a formal letter of reference supporting a former student's application to a university programme. Describe their background, achievements and personal qualities.
11.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de recomendación para un exalumno que se postula a un programa universitario: contexto, logros y cualidades personales.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Members of the Admissions Committee, a clear purpose in the first sentence, a firm recommendation and Yours faithfully.
At least five compound adjectives (hard-working, open-minded, self-taught, low-cost, kind-hearted…) and at least one superlative compound (one of the most hard-working…).
At least three words from the unit (against all odds, determined, resilient, groundbreaking).
11.model:
Dear Members of the Admissions Committee,

I am pleased to write in support of Camilo Reyes's application to your engineering programme. I am writing in my capacity as his physics teacher and head of department. I have taught Camilo for three years, and I can say without hesitation that he is one of the most hard-working and open-minded students I have met in twenty years of teaching.

Camilo comes from a low-income family in a town where few young people finish secondary school. Against all odds, he has maintained the highest grades in his year while working weekends in his uncle's workshop. Largely self-taught in electronics, he built a low-cost water-quality sensor for his final-year project, which won first prize at the regional science fair. The device is now used by two local farming cooperatives.

Beyond his academic ability, Camilo is a determined and resilient person. When his project failed its first three tests, he did not give up; he analysed the data, asked for advice and tried again. He is also generous with his time: for two years he has run a free after-school club in which younger pupils learn to build simple circuits. His classmates, who regard him as a natural leader, describe him as down-to-earth and kind-hearted.

I have no doubt that Camilo will make a groundbreaking contribution to your programme and, in time, to his profession. I recommend him without reservation. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you require further information.

Yours faithfully,
Beatriz Cano
Head of Physics

11.title: Presenting the Teacher of the Year award
11.brief: Write a speech to present a Teacher of the Year award at a school ceremony. Describe the winner's qualities, give examples and end by inviting the audience to applaud.
11.briefEs: Escribe un discurso para entregar el premio al Profesor del Año en una ceremonia escolar: cualidades, ejemplos y un cierre que invite a aplaudir.
criteria: At least five compound adjectives (big-hearted, hands-on, thought-provoking, long-lasting…) and at least one superlative compound (the longest-serving).
At least three expressions from the unit (role model, to look up to, legacy, resilient, determined).
A spoken register with direct address, concrete examples and a closing sentence that invites applause.
11.model:
Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you all for being here to celebrate the Teacher of the Year award.

Every school has someone who is, quite simply, a role model. Someone whom pupils look up to, even if they would never admit it. This year, our winner is Mr Ernesto Valencia, who has taught history at our school for twenty-six years.

Mr Valencia is the longest-serving member of our staff, but that is not why he is here tonight. He is here because he is the kind of teacher who remembers every pupil's name, even years later. He is a big-hearted, hands-on teacher who once drove two hours in the rain to return a lost notebook the night before an exam.

His classes are never dull. He has turned the Battle of Boyacá into a role-play, taught the Industrial Revolution through a cooking competition and persuaded sixty teenagers to spend a Saturday cleaning a historic cemetery. Parents tell me that their children come home with thought-provoking questions, which is a rare and wonderful achievement.

Many of his former pupils are now doctors, engineers and teachers themselves. They are his legacy, and it is a long-lasting one. When asked what he is proudest of, he said: 'The moment a pupil who thought they were bad at history realises they are not.'

Ladies and gentlemen, please join me in applauding our Teacher of the Year, Mr Ernesto Valencia.

12.title: Is entrepreneurship overrated?
12.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether young people are being encouraged too strongly to start their own businesses instead of seeking stable employment.
12.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si se presiona demasiado a los jóvenes para emprender en lugar de buscar empleo estable.
criteria: Two conditionals with inversion (Were…, Had…, Should…).
Three adverb clauses of condition (provided that, unless, as long as, on condition that).
Use “startup”, “to break even” and “to get off the ground”.
12.model:
Social media is full of young founders who claim to have built million-dollar companies from their bedrooms. Universities run entrepreneurship programmes, and governments promote startups as the solution to unemployment. But is this enthusiasm justified?

There are undeniable benefits to entrepreneurship. New businesses create jobs, drive innovation and allow people to pursue their passions. In Colombia, where formal employment is scarce for many graduates, starting a company may be the only way to earn a decent income. Provided that founders have a viable idea and some financial support, the experience of building something can be invaluable, even if the business eventually fails.

However, the risks are rarely discussed honestly. The majority of startups close within five years, and many never break even. Were young people better informed about these statistics, fewer of them would invest their savings — or their parents' — in untested ideas. Getting a business off the ground also requires skills that most graduates have not yet developed: managing cash flow, negotiating with suppliers, hiring staff. Had I started a company at twenty-two, I suspect I would have learned these lessons the hard way.

In my view, entrepreneurship should be presented as one option among many, not as the only path to success. Working for an established organisation first allows people to gain experience and contacts. As long as they keep their ambitions alive, there is nothing to stop them launching their own venture later, with far better chances. Unless we stop glorifying the founder myth, we risk setting a generation up for disappointment.

12.title: Negotiating a better offer
12.brief: You have received a job offer but want to negotiate the conditions (salary, remote work, start date). Write a formal email to the employer.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal negociando las condiciones de una oferta de trabajo (salario, teletrabajo, fecha de inicio).
criteria: One conditional with inversion (Should you need…, Were it possible…).
Two adverb clauses of condition (provided that, on condition that, as long as).
A professional, confident but courteous tone.
12.model:
Dear Ms. Salgado,

Thank you very much for offering me the position of Senior Data Analyst at Andina Logistics. I was delighted to receive your letter, and I remain very enthusiastic about the opportunity to join your team.

Before formally accepting, I would like to discuss two aspects of the offer. Firstly, regarding the salary, I note that the proposed figure is somewhat below the market rate for similar roles in Bogotá, according to recent industry surveys. Given my eight years of experience and my expertise in supply-chain forecasting, I would like to ask whether it would be possible to increase the base salary by 12%. I would be happy to consider a smaller increase provided that it were reviewed after a six-month probation period.

Secondly, I would greatly appreciate the opportunity to work remotely two days a week. In my current role, this arrangement has allowed me to be considerably more productive, and I am confident it would not affect my availability for meetings, as long as these are scheduled in advance.

Were it possible to agree on these points, I would be ready to start on 1 March, as originally planned. Should you need any further information about my previous projects or references, please do not hesitate to contact me.

I look forward to your response and, I hope, to working with you.

Yours sincerely,
Daniel Morales

12.title: The ideal job: a reflective essay
12.brief: Write a personal essay describing your ideal job and the conditions under which you would accept compromises (salary, location, hours).
12.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo personal sobre tu trabajo ideal y bajo qué condiciones aceptarías hacer concesiones.
criteria: Two inverted conditionals and three adverb clauses of condition.
Use “to think outside the box”, “to scale back” and “to be in the black”.
A reflective tone with a thoughtful conclusion.
12.model:
When I was a child, my ideal job changed every week: astronaut, footballer, vet. Today, my answer is less glamorous but considerably more detailed.

My ideal job would allow me to think outside the box. I am happiest when I am solving problems that do not have obvious answers, so I would rather design something new than manage something that already exists. I would also want my work to have a visible impact — ideally in education or public health, where good ideas can change thousands of lives.

The people matter as much as the tasks. I would accept a modest salary on condition that I worked with colleagues who were generous with their knowledge and honest in their criticism. Had I been asked this question five years ago, I would have put money first. Experience has taught me that a toxic team can ruin even the best-paid position.

Of course, ideals have limits. I have to pay rent, and I would like to help my parents in the future. Unless a job paid enough for me to be in the black at the end of each month, I could not take it, however inspiring it was. Should the perfect opportunity appear in another city, I would be willing to move, provided that I could return home regularly.

Perhaps the ideal job is less a fixed destination than a direction. If I ever had to scale back my ambitions, I would hope to do so without losing sight of why I started: to do work that matters, with people I respect.

12.title: Should remote work be the default for office jobs?
12.brief: C1+ / puente a C2. Write an academic essay on whether remote work should become the default arrangement for office jobs. Weigh the benefits for employees and companies against the risks, and propose a compromise.
12.briefEs: C1+ / puente a C2. Escribe un ensayo académico sobre si el trabajo remoto debería ser la norma en empleos de oficina, con ventajas, riesgos y una propuesta intermedia.
criteria: At least three conditionals with inversion, including Had it not been for… or Were it not for… (C1+ structures) and one with Were… to or Should….
At least three adverb clauses of condition (provided that, unless, on condition that, as long as, even if).
At least two expressions from the unit (startup, to break even, to think outside the box) and a balanced conclusion.
12.model:
Before 2020, working from home was a rare privilege. Had it not been for the pandemic, many companies would probably still be insisting on a physical presence from nine to five. Today, the question is whether remote work should remain the default for office jobs or whether employees should return to the workplace.

The advantages of remote work are well documented. Employees save hours of commuting, and many report higher concentration at home, provided that they have a quiet space. A startup with a limited budget, for example, may be able to break even months earlier if it does not need to rent an office.

However, the model has limits. Were remote work to become universal, newcomers would lose the informal learning that happens in corridors and at lunch tables, and isolation could harm mental health. Creativity, too, may suffer: it is difficult to think outside the box when one's only colleagues are faces on a screen. Should a team be spread across several time zones, coordination becomes even harder. Unless companies invest consciously in culture, remote employees may feel invisible when promotions are decided.

A hybrid arrangement therefore seems the most sensible compromise. Employees could work from home on condition that they attend the office for key meetings, as long as the schedule is agreed in advance. Were it not for the risk of isolation, full remote work would be the better option; since the risk is real, a balance is preferable. Even if every task could be done online, human contact remains part of what makes work meaningful.

12.title: Report: a pilot of the four-day working week
12.brief: Write a report for the board of a company on a six-month pilot of a four-day working week in one department. Present the results and recommend whether to extend the arrangement.
12.briefEs: Escribe un informe para la junta de una empresa sobre un piloto de seis meses de semana laboral de cuatro días en un departamento, con una recomendación.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations and Conclusion.
At least three conditionals with inversion (Had a rota been introduced…, Should the results be similar…, Were the company to…).
At least three adverb clauses of condition (provided that, unless, in case, as long as) and two expressions from the unit (in the black, to scale back).
12.model:
Report: A Pilot of the Four-Day Working Week

Introduction
This report assesses a six-month pilot of a four-day working week in the marketing department of Textiles del Valle, involving fourteen employees. Its purpose is to decide whether the arrangement should be extended to the whole company.

Findings
Productivity, measured by completed projects, remained stable, and absenteeism fell by almost a third. Staff turnover, which had been high in the previous year, fell to zero during the pilot. Employees reported lower stress and said that they would be reluctant to return to a five-day week unless their salaries rose substantially. Clients, however, were less enthusiastic: three complained that they had difficulty contacting the team on Fridays. Had a rota been introduced from the start, this problem might have been avoided. The company remained in the black throughout the pilot, although overtime costs increased slightly in the second quarter.

Recommendations
We recommend that the arrangement be extended to the sales department as a second trial, provided that a staggered rota guarantees cover on all five days. Should the results be similar, it could then be adopted company-wide. Were the company to scale back its client-facing hours, however, revenue could suffer, so no reduction in availability should be accepted. Managers should be briefed in case staff raise concerns about workload.

Conclusion
On the evidence of this pilot, a shorter week is a viable option. As long as client service is protected, the benefits for staff wellbeing are likely to outweigh the costs.

12.title: A microloan fund for young entrepreneurs
12.brief: Write a proposal to the municipality for a microloan fund that helps young people start small businesses. Explain the problem, the conditions of the loans, the budget and the expected results.
12.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al municipio para un fondo de microcréditos que ayude a jóvenes a crear pequeños negocios.
criteria: Headings: Background, Proposal, Budget and Expected results.
At least three conditionals with inversion (Had a scheme existed…, Should a borrower…, Were additional donors to join…).
At least three adverb clauses of condition (on condition that, provided that, as long as, unless, even if) and two expressions from the unit (startup, to get off the ground, to break even).
12.model:
Proposal: A Microloan Fund for Young Entrepreneurs

Background
Many young people in our town have viable business ideas, but banks will not lend them money because they have no credit history or collateral. As a result, promising startups never get off the ground. Had a lending scheme existed three years ago, several local ventures that closed would probably have survived.

Proposal
We propose a revolving fund of COP 120,000,000, from which loans of up to COP 6,000,000 would be granted to applicants aged eighteen to thirty. Loans would be approved on condition that applicants complete a short business-planning course and present a realistic cash-flow forecast. Repayments would begin six months after the loan is granted, provided that the business has started trading. Should a borrower run into difficulty, the repayment schedule could be renegotiated, as long as the borrower informs the committee promptly.

Budget
The fund would be financed by contributions from the municipality and local businesses. Administration costs, estimated at 8 per cent of the fund, would cover a part-time coordinator. Were additional donors to join, the number of loans could be increased.

Expected results
We expect around twenty businesses to receive support in the first year, and at least half to break even within eighteen months. Even if some fail, the fund would continue to circulate, since repayments from successful ventures would finance new loans. Unless young entrepreneurs are given a first chance, the town will continue to lose its most creative people to larger cities. Should the pilot succeed, we would be glad to share our results with other municipalities.

12.title: Review: a memoir of a failed startup
12.brief: Write a critical review of a memoir or business book, real or imagined, in which an entrepreneur describes a company that failed. Evaluate its honesty, its advice and its usefulness for readers.
12.briefEs: Escribe una reseña crítica de unas memorias o un libro de negocios, real o imaginado, en el que un emprendedor cuenta el fracaso de su empresa.
criteria: At least three conditionals with inversion (Had she listened…, Were she to…, Should you…).
At least two adverb clauses of condition (even if, provided that, unless, as long as).
At least three expressions from the unit (startup, to close a deal, to get off the ground, to scale back, to break even, to think outside the box) and a final rating.
12.model:
In Out of Cash, Mariana Toro recounts the rise and fall of Cuenta Clara, a financial-education startup she founded at twenty-four. It is a candid, often funny memoir, and it deserves to be read by anyone who dreams of starting a company.

Toro is admirably honest about her mistakes. Had she listened to her first adviser, she writes, she would have avoided hiring twelve people before the product existed. Her description of the day the company almost closed a deal with a major bank, only to lose it over a missing document, is gripping. The book is at its best when it conveys the loneliness of leadership. Toro never pretends that thinking outside the box is a comfortable experience.

The book is weaker when it offers advice. Several chapters read like motivational posters, and the lessons Toro draws from her failure, such as 'listen to your customers' and 'never stop learning', are hardly original. Were she to scale back the self-help passages and trust her story, the book would be stronger. I also wished for more detail about the finances: we are told that the startup never managed to break even, but not why.

Nevertheless, Out of Cash is a valuable corrective to the glamorous image of entrepreneurship. Should you be considering a startup of your own, read it first. Even if you disagree with its advice, you will enjoy it, provided that you read it critically. It will not tell you how to get off the ground, but it will tell you what the ground feels like when you hit it. Four stars out of five.

12.title: Application for a business loan
12.brief: Write a formal letter to a bank applying for a business loan to expand a small company. Describe the business, explain what the money would be used for and offer guarantees.
12.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal a un banco solicitando un préstamo para ampliar un pequeño negocio: descripción, uso del dinero y garantías.
criteria: Formal conventions: Dear Mr…, a clear request in the opening sentence, enclosures and Yours sincerely.
At least three conditionals with inversion (Were I able to…, Should the bank require…, Had it not been for…).
At least three adverb clauses of condition (provided that, even if, unless, as long as) and two expressions from the unit (in the black, to get off the ground, to close a deal).
12.model:
Dear Mr Villegas,

I am writing to apply for a business loan of COP 45,000,000 to expand my bakery, Pan de Casa, which I have run in Ibagué for four years.

The business is in the black and has been since its second year. Monthly sales have grown by an average of 6 per cent, and I now employ five people. However, our single oven limits production, and we are regularly forced to turn away large orders from local restaurants. Were I able to double our capacity, I am confident that we could close several of the contracts we are currently unable to accept.

The loan would be used to buy a second oven and to rent the adjacent premises. According to my projections, the investment would pay for itself within two years, provided that sales continue to grow at the current rate. Even if growth were to slow, the business would still be able to meet its repayments, as I have prepared a conservative forecast, which is enclosed with this letter.

I would be willing to offer the bakery equipment as security. Should the bank require additional guarantees, I would be glad to discuss them. I would also appreciate the chance to meet you in person, unless you consider this unnecessary at this stage.

Had it not been for the support of my customers, the bakery would never have got off the ground, and I would like to repay their loyalty by growing responsibly. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Laura Sánchez

12.title: Opening speech for a young entrepreneurs' final
12.brief: Write the opening speech for the final of a school competition in which student teams present business ideas. Congratulate the teams, share three lessons and encourage the audience.
12.briefEs: Escribe el discurso de apertura de la final de un concurso escolar de ideas de negocio: felicita a los equipos, comparte tres lecciones y anima al público.
criteria: At least three conditionals with inversion (Had they done so…, Should you ever think…, Were I to list…).
At least three adverb clauses of condition (unless, as long as, even if, provided that).
At least three expressions from the unit (startup, to close a deal, to get off the ground, to think outside the box) and a spoken register with a clear structure (three lessons).
12.model:
Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the final of the Young Entrepreneurs Challenge.

Six teams have reached this stage. Each of them has spent four months turning an idea into a prototype, and each of them has, at some point, wanted to give up. Several of them stayed after school until the caretaker asked them to leave. Had they done so, we would not be here today.

Let me tell you what I have learned from watching these teams. First, a good idea is not enough. Unless you can explain it to a stranger in thirty seconds, you will struggle to close a deal. Second, nobody gets a startup off the ground alone. Should you ever think that you can do everything yourself, remember the mentors, parents and friends who are sitting in this room.

Third, and most importantly, failure is part of the process. Were I to list every mistake these teams have made, we would be here until midnight. But a startup that never fails is a startup that never tries anything new. As long as you learn from each setback, you are moving forward, even if it does not feel that way.

Tonight, one team will win. Whoever it is, the prize will be money for the prototype, but the real reward is something else: the confidence to think outside the box. Provided that you keep that confidence, none of you will leave this room empty-handed.

Good luck to all six teams. Let the final begin.
